skeleton: garrison must split scarce force between a port and a depot joined by one causeway while raiders can bypass the road entirely, hide inside civilian traffic, and every pre-emptive disruption is punished unless vindicated
inspiration: British anti-infiltration garrisoning of the Malayan coastal kampongs and causeways, 1948-1950 (Malayan Emergency)
title: OPERATION IRON LANTERN
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} border, {YEAR}. Your command is taking over the defense of a single supply line. The fen causeway is the only all-weather road between the DropPort and the depot town — fourteen kilometers long and six meters wide — and every ton of rice, peat, and ammunition the district moves travels along it. On either side of the road is the fen: 1,100 square kilometers of black water, reed islands, and seasonal mud deep enough to swallow a 40-ton machine up to the hip during the wet months. {EMPLOYER} gives your command garrison authority over the causeway, the depot, and the picket line, taking over from a militia company that served 26 months without an attack. The ISF resident has added a note to the handover file: those 26 quiet months are a warning, not a reassurance — a patient raider has had that long to study the garrison's habits. You inherit this routine: picket posts at causeway Markers 3, 6, 9, and 12, each held by 4 militia infantry on 6-hour watches; one armor section (2 Scorpion light tanks) at the depot; and your lance, the only BattleMech force within 300 kilometers. Two things make the enemy hard to see. First, fen mist: between 0300 and 0700, on 8 mornings out of 10, thermal imaging works only out to about 400 meters. Second, buried Star League-era dredging machinery, which produces 3 to 7 false magscan contacts every night. The local people are the fen-cutters: 4,100 civilians in stilt hamlets who cut peat, run barges, and watch everything. Assume the barge crews know about any move your garrison makes within 12 hours. They are not loyal to you, but they are not against you either. {NPC:intel-source} reports a {TARGET_FACTION} raiding force loading aboard a chartered merchant DropShip two systems coreward: an estimated {RAIDER_LANCES} lance(s) with hover armor support. That report is 9 days old, so the force may already be closer than it says. Hover armor does not need the causeway: it can cross the open fen at speed in any season, and your BattleMechs cannot follow it off the road during the wet months. The depot holds the district's 90-day rice reserve and 210 tons of garrison munitions. Holding the road but losing the depot counts as failure. The job is the watch itself — count the barge lanterns, keep the log, send someone out to confirm each ghost contact is only a buried dredge head — every night, until the night it is a raid.

objectives.primary: Keep the depot secure for the length of the contract. If it is attacked, at least 75 percent of the rice reserve and the munition stores must survive.
objectives.secondary: Keep the causeway open to traffic. It may not be blocked for more than 24 hours in a row.
objectives.bonus: Capture or identify the raiders' local guide. The ISF resident will repay this with favors that carry real weight.

complications.name: Fen Mist Window
complications.text: Between 0300 and 0700, mist drops thermal sensor range to under 400 meters across the fen and the causeway. A raid is four times more likely to come during this window than at any other time, because the poor visibility favors the attacker. The militia pickets know this and sleep badly because of it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During mist turns, halve all sensor and visual detection ranges. The attacker may also place units in hidden deployment within the fen.

complications.name: Ghost Returns
complications.text: Buried dredging machinery produces 3 to 7 false magscan contacts every night. Each alarm has to be checked in person by a picket or a 'Mech, because there is no way to tell a ghost contact from a real one on sensors alone. Your command has already been doing this for three weeks when the mission begins.
complications.mechanicalEffect: At each alarm, roll 1d6. On 1-3 the first reported contact is a false one, and any unit sent to investigate it starts the real engagement out of position for the first 2 turns.

complications.name: Barge Traffic Screen
complications.text: Peat barges move through the fen channels day and night, 20 to 30 of them at any given hour. Hover armor traveling at barge speed inside a channel looks exactly like ordinary traffic on sensors — you cannot tell them apart until you see them with your own eyes. Shutting down all barge traffic would choke the district's economy and break the rice delivery schedule.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The attacker's hover units may enter the map disguised as neutral barge traffic. They are revealed only by inspection at visual range or when they open fire. If the defender shuts down barge traffic before any attack, apply the No-Incident Audit penalty immediately.

complications.name: No-Incident Audit
complications.text: The ISF resident writes a weekly report on your command. Disruptive measures taken before any attack — shutting down barges, pressing fen-cutters into service, abandoning a picket post — are recorded as a loss of nerve, unless an attack actually follows within 7 days and proves the measure was justified.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each disruptive measure taken before an attack applies a cumulative -1 to the end-of-mission employer-standing roll, unless a raid occurs within 7 days of that measure.

decisionPoints.name: Basing the Lance
decisionPoints.context: Your lance cannot reach both ends of a 14-kilometer causeway quickly enough, especially in fen mist. You can base at the DropPort, base at the depot, or split your force between them — each is a reasonable choice. Whatever you decide, the militia will take its confidence from yours.

options.title: Base at the DropPort
advantages: You can react fast along the causeway's hard surface at full speed
You protect the only off-world evacuation point and keep access to your own DropShip
disadvantages: The depot is 14 kilometers away — more than 11 minutes at flank speed
The militia at the depot will see this as abandonment, and their watch discipline will slip
options.consequence: If the raid hits the depot directly, you arrive late and a few machines at a time, fighting only the last third of the battle. Militia morale takes a -1 modifier for the engagement.

costs.risk: You secure the port but leave the depot exposed: every alarm there is answered more than 11 minutes and 14 kilometers late

options.title: Base at the Depot
advantages: The primary objective sits inside your perimeter at all times
Militia watch standards improve measurably with 'Mechs in the compound
disadvantages: A raid on the DropPort, or a blown causeway, cuts you off from resupply and evacuation
Reaching the far causeway markers takes more than 12 minutes
options.consequence: The depot is much more likely to survive, but a skilled raider will blow the causeway bridge at Marker 3 first, leaving you to fight with no way to retreat.

costs.resource: militia labor: 5 days of digging revetments and berms inside the depot compound
costs.risk: If the Marker 3 bridge is demolished, the lance fights with no line of retreat and no resupply

options.title: Split: Two and Two
advantages: No single point of failure: either pair can fight a delaying action
A presence at both ends keeps the militia and the port workers steady
disadvantages: Neither pair can beat a full raiding lance on its own
Commanding and coordinating two pairs across 14 kilometers of mist is the hardest part of the battle
options.consequence: Every fight starts with two of your units against the raiders' concentrated force. Whether the other pair arrives in time to even the odds depends on the reaction timeline.

costs.resource: double the watch overhead: fuel and coolant must be hauled to two sites 14 kilometers apart
costs.risk: Whichever pair the raiders hit fights their full force alone until the other pair can cross the mist to help

entries.event: Picket alarm: Marker 9 reports engine noise in the fen channels but no visual contact. The mist window is active.

Your ready 'Mechs move out and the militia armor section starts its engines. The Marker 6 picket reports barge lanterns scattering — civilian craft clearing the channels, which means they know something is in the water.
Raider hover units can now reach any point along the causeway embankment from the open fen. This is the earliest you can realistically confirm their strength by sight.
Your blocking position at Marker 6 must be occupied by now to stand between the raiders and the approach to the depot.
If a raider 'Mech element was landed on the north shore by lander, it finishes its march to the causeway junction at this point.
If no one has blocked them, the raiders reach the depot gates and start setting demolition charges. The rice and munition stores are now within direct-fire range.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Your blocking force must hold Marker 6 by T+14:00. If it does not, the raiders reach the depot stores at T+26:00 and the primary objective fails — the stores are destroyed by demolition before you can fight for them.

opforSketch.composition: One raiding lance of fast medium 'Mechs (40-55 tons, jump-capable preferred) at Regular-to-Veteran quality, supported by 4-6 hover armor vehicles (behaving like Saracen/Saladin-class units) and 1 platoon of mechanized infantry acting as a demolition party. No aerospace beyond the lander that drops them off.
opforSketch.behavior: Raiders, not conquerors. They avoid the garrison's strength, pin it in place with the hover vehicles, hit the depot with the 'Mech element, burn whatever they cannot carry off, and withdraw across the fen before the militia armor can close in. The 'Mechs and hover units break off the fight once they have taken 40 percent damage; the demolition party keeps working regardless.

forks.name: OPERATION LANTERN COUNT
forks.trigger: Depot held with stores intact and at least one raider prisoner or wreck recovered for ISF examination.
forks.consequence: The ISF resident traces the raiders' local guide to a barge consortium and contracts your command for the quiet arrest sweep — a SECURITY_DUTY follow-on among the same fen-cutters who fed you tea on the picket line.

forks.name: OPERATION ASH PADDY
forks.trigger: Depot stores destroyed or reduced below 75 percent.
forks.consequence: The district faces a 90-day rice deficit; {EMPLOYER} orders your command to escort emergency grain convoys down the same causeway while the population's patience thins — RELIEF_DUTY under hostile observation, threat elevated.

forks.name: OPERATION STILL WATER
forks.trigger: Depot held but the causeway blocked for more than 24 hours, or stores between 50 and 75 percent.
forks.consequence: The raiders' hover element went to ground in the fen instead of withdrawing. Two weeks of intermittent sabotage follow until someone hunts them through the channels at visual range.

storyElementSeed: Night watch at Marker 9: a sentry counts barge lanterns out on the black water and writes the number in the log, because last week the count was nine and tonight it is eleven, and the log does not care which lanterns are honest.

merc.objectives.primary: The contract requires the depot to keep at least 75 percent of its stock for full payment, and the employer's auditors will literally weigh the rice. Closing the causeway for more than 24 hours triggers the performance-penalty clause in Section 11. Read that section before you move anything.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Hold the depot with 75 percent of its stock or better when the fighting ends. That number is the mission. The causeway matters because the depot's supplies flow through it, so keep the road open and the warehouse standing. Put more effort into the road day to day, but the warehouse is the higher priority if you have to choose.

MIST_MORNINGS_PER_10.unit: mornings per 10 with active mist window

resourceGates.lackingText: If your unit has no DropShip on the hardstand, the berth fee drops to 2,000 C-bills, but you lose the evacuation advantage: any lift now depends on {EMPLOYER}'s schedule, and arranging your own charter would cost roughly 40,000 C-bills.

phases.name: POSTURE — THE WATCH
phases.lead: The garrison's 26 quiet months end the moment you take over. Spend the first weeks learning the causeway's normal patterns — lantern counts, ghost contacts, barge schedules — until your command can tell a normal night from a suspicious one on its own, without waking the duty officer.

dataBlock.Mist window: 0300-0700 local, thermal range under 400m, 8 mornings in 10
dataBlock.Ghost returns: 3-7 false magscan contacts per night off buried dredge machinery — every one walked out and logged
dataBlock.Barge baseline: 20-30 hulls moving at any hour; evening lantern count logged at each marker at 30-minute intervals
dataBlock.Reaction arithmetic: Depot to Marker 6: 12 minutes at flank on the roadbed; DropPort to depot: 11-plus minutes

phases.protocol: Lantern tally: every 30 minutes, each picket counts the visible barge lanterns and compares the count to that evening's baseline. A change of 2 or more lanterns in either direction is reported by landline, not radio. The codeword BLACK REED, sent in plain language on the garrison net, means a hover unit has been confirmed by eye. On that word, every station stands to and the armor section starts its engines without waiting for further orders.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why 26 months without an attack is a warning rather than a reassurance: what a patient raid planner can do with 26 months spent studying a garrison's habits.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — THE NIGHT THE COUNT IS WRONG
phases.lead: The raid comes during the mist window, hidden among the barge traffic, and forces your lance to choose between defending the depot and holding the causeway while the clock runs. The one fixed requirement is to hold Marker 6 by T+14:00; arrange everything else in the fight around that.

dataBlock.Blocking position: Marker 6 embankment — roadbed 6m wide, the one point where fen channels on both flanks keep hover armor from bypassing at speed
dataBlock.Occupation deadline: T+14:00; raider hover elements can touch the embankment anywhere from T+8:00
dataBlock.Demolition exposure: Unblocked raiders at depot gates T+26:00; stores in direct-fire range from that point
dataBlock.Mist combat ranges: Detection halved; visual identification of barge versus hover at under 400m only

sidebarKernel.kernel: Fighting a delaying action on a 6-meter roadbed: why the second 'Mech in the column is the one that decides the fight, and why backing up under fire on the narrow causeway has to be practiced before the night it is needed.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — THE FEN SETTLES
phases.lead: The causeway has to carry traffic again within 24 hours of the last shot, or the secondary objective fails even though you won the fight. Anything the fen left behind — wrecks, prisoners, a guide who knew the channels — must be collected before the water and the fen-cutters take it back.

dataBlock.Causeway reopening: 24-hour ceiling on blockage; wreck clearance on a 6m roadbed runs 3-5 hours per hull with depot recovery gear
dataBlock.Stock audit: Rice and munitions counted against the 75 percent threshold within 48 hours — the ISF resident attends the count
dataBlock.Recovery window: Hover wrecks in the fen are strippable by barge crews within 12 hours of settling; anything the ISF wants examined is guarded or gone

sidebarKernel.kernel: The audit arithmetic: what 75 percent of 90 days of rice means measured against the district's winter, and why the count is witnessed.

skeleton: garrison must block a terrain back door that opens on a publicly printed environmental cycle while its own repeating dispositions and a flood of sincere false reports leak its posture
inspiration: Wehrmacht tidal-defence of the Scheldt estuary causeways, Walcheren 1944
title: OPERATION WINTER CENSUS
situation: {WORLD}, {YEAR}. The district you are assigned to held 900,000 people before the massacre. The last census counted 61,000. Your posting is the valley: one working fusion plant, four resettlement granaries, and 70 kilometers of river line, backed by the burned-out shell of the river city — which nobody patrols after dark, because the survivors have asked them not to. {EMPLOYER} wants two things kept running through the winter: the plant and the grain. In the past 14 months, {TARGET_FACTION} raiders have hit power infrastructure on 2 other resettlement worlds in this march. That pattern is 21 days old and well confirmed, so treat the plant as a likely next target. The main terrain problem is the estuary tide flats. Twice during each 22.4-hour tidal cycle the estuary drains, and for a 3-hour window the mud is firm enough to carry hover vehicles and 'Mechs under 60 tons across 9 kilometers of water that is otherwise impassable. That crossing leads directly behind the plant's southern fence — a back door. Outside that window, the flats are a drowning hazard that has already claimed one militia scout car this year (the crew got out; the vehicle did not). The flats cannot be effectively mined, because the tide moves anything lighter than 200 kilograms. You inherit this patrol routine: 2 militia infantry platoons walking the granary perimeters on 8-hour rotations, 1 platoon at the plant, and your lance split between the plant hardstand and a ready position on the ferry hill, which overlooks the flats from 4 kilometers away. Sensors are unreliable here: the ruined city scatters structural-collapse echoes across magscan, and survivors light salvage fires at random hours, so you cannot confirm a thermal contact inside the ruins without walking in to check. The harder problem is the people. They report everything — every light on the water, every stranger, every aircraft. Their hatred of the Dragon is complete and their eagerness is genuine, but when this quarter's reports were reviewed, 70 percent turned out to be ferry traffic, salvagers, or grief. You cannot ignore the reports, because the other 30 percent are real. {NPC:intel-source} reads the threat as a fuel-raid pattern: a light raiding force working from a hidden forward fuel point within 200 kilometers, striking on the nights when the tide window and the dark of the moons line up. That happens on 4 nights out of every 28 ({TIDE_DARK_NIGHTS} of them this month, according to the almanac your operations sergeant now keeps taped above the duty desk).

objectives.primary: Keep the fusion plant running for the length of the contract. No damage to the reactor hall, turbine line, or switchyard may take more than 14 days to repair.
objectives.secondary: Keep all four resettlement granaries intact. No granary may lose more than 10 percent of its stored grain.
objectives.bonus: Find the raiders' forward fuel cache, using pursuit evidence, a prisoner's statement, or data recovered from a wreck.

complications.name: The Almanac Problem
complications.text: The dates when the tide window and the moon-dark line up are printed in every civil almanac on the planet. The raiders can read them just as easily as you can, and so can any civilian trying to guess where your lance will be on those 4 nights. The danger is your own predictability: if you defend the same way every alignment night, you teach the enemy your plan.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the defender uses the same deployment positions on alignment nights more than twice, the attacker gets one free repositioning move before the battle and chooses which map edge to enter from.

complications.name: Eager Sources
complications.text: Civilian reports come in at 5 to 12 per week, and you cannot simply ignore them, even though 7 in 10 turn out to be nothing. Every report a patrol goes out to check costs fuel and crew rest, and leaves a granary perimeter covered only by the militia while the patrol is away.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Before the engagement, roll 1d6. On 1-2, one defending unit starts the battle off the map because it is returning from checking a false report; it arrives at the end of turn 2 on the defender's home edge.

complications.name: Survivors in the Ruin Line
complications.text: Salvage parties from the resettlement camps work the ruined city without permits, and without showing any lights you could spot. If a fight moves into the ruins, it puts these civilians at risk. A single civilian death on {WORLD} would carry political consequences far beyond anything this brief can measure.
complications.mechanicalEffect: After deployment, the gamemaster secretly places 1d3 hidden civilian salvage parties in hexes within the ruin line. Any area-effect or building-collapse damage in those hexes immediately applies an employer-standing penalty and ends your eligibility for the bonus objective.

decisionPoints.name: The Back Door
decisionPoints.context: The tide flats cannot be mined, and they cannot be ignored. The ferry hill overlooks them, but watching is not the same as blocking, and the 3-hour window is long enough for a fast force to cross, hit the plant's south fence, and cross back — if nothing stands in its way.

options.title: Picket the Flats Directly
advantages: Any crossing is met at the water line, where the raiders are moving slowest
You are certain to detect a crossing during the window — nothing gets across unseen
disadvantages: The picket unit sits in tidal mud on a hard 3-hour clock, with no way out once the water comes back
One unit is tied up every alignment night, wearing down the crews over time
options.consequence: Crossings are stopped or badly hurt at the shore, but the picket fights alone for the first 6 minutes of any engagement, and the tide returns on schedule no matter how the fight is going.

costs.resource: picket fatigue: one unit tied up every alignment night, 4 nights in 28
costs.risk: The tide has already claimed one vehicle this year; a badly timed withdrawal will cost you another

options.title: Hold the ferry hill, React on Contact
advantages: The lance fights as one group, from high ground, on dry footing
No unit is caught out on the tide clock
disadvantages: The 4-kilometer reaction distance means you give up the south fence as the battleground
Mist or thermal clutter from salvage fires can delay your confirmation until it is too late to intercept
options.consequence: The fight happens at the plant fence against raiders who are already in position, and the plant takes some damage in any exchange of fire there.

costs.risk: No C-bill cost; the price is the 4-kilometer reaction distance — the south fence becomes the battleground and the plant takes the stray fire

options.title: Leave It Open, Wire It for Sound
advantages: Seismic and acoustic sensors need no personnel and never get tired
Letting the raiders cross unopposed draws them into a fight on ground you chose, between the flats and the fence
disadvantages: The sensors confirm that a crossing happened but not how strong it is or what it is made of
If the enemy guesses your ambush position — or is told where it is — the trap turns against you
options.consequence: The fight begins with the raiders ashore and committed, facing your full force at a spot you picked. Everything depends on your ambush holding its fire until the right moment.

costs.risk: If the ambush position is guessed or betrayed, the trap turns against you

entries.event: Alarm: a seismic sensor or the ferry hill watch confirms vehicles on the flats, heading in. The tide window is open with 2 hours 40 minutes left.
Your ready element moves out from the ferry hill, and the plant's militia platoon takes up fighting positions on the south fence.
If unopposed, the raiders' lead units finish the 9-kilometer crossing and reach the south fence line.
From this point, the raiders can place demolition charges on the switchyard transformers. Each 5 minutes they hold the yard means one more transformer rigged to blow.
This is 105 minutes before the tide turns. The raiders must start crossing back by now, or give up the flats route and fight their way out overland.
The tide window closes. Anything still on the flats — theirs or yours — is lost to the water.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The switchyard must be cleared of raiders by T+25:00. If it is not, they start destroying transformers at one every 5 minutes; once 3 transformers are destroyed the plant can no longer carry the district's winter load, and the primary objective fails.

opforSketch.composition: A fast raiding force built around the tide window: 3-5 hover armor vehicles, 1 light 'Mech lance (20-45 tons, nothing over 55, which is the flats' weight limit), and 1 engineer demolition squad in a hover APC. Regular quality, with the worn, scavenged equipment typical of early Succession Wars shortages.
opforSketch.behavior: Driven by the clock. Every move is timed against the tide. They will not commit to a stand-up fight, and they break for the flats the moment their window to cross back starts to run out, leaving damaged vehicles behind. The demolition squad is the whole point of the raid, so the rest of the force protects it throughout.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY SLIP
forks.trigger: Plant and granaries intact, and pursuit evidence or prisoners taken.
forks.consequence: Wreck telemetry points to the forward fuel cache in the coastal barrens 140 kilometers south — a RECON_RAID follow-on to find and burn it before the next alignment nights.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG DARK
forks.trigger: Three or more transformers destroyed, or reactor hall damaged.
forks.consequence: The valley loses winter power for 60-plus days. Resettlement camps fall back on salvage fires and patience runs out; your command keeps order at the relief distribution points through the cold — RIOT_DUTY among people who have already survived worse than you.

forks.name: OPERATION EBB MARKER
forks.trigger: Plant held but raiders extracted across the flats with under 25 percent losses.
forks.consequence: They will be back on the next alignment — 24 to 28 days out — with your dispositions in their after-action file. Same ground, fewer surprises, threat raised one band.

storyElementSeed: A patrol halts at a farmstead where one lamp burns; the family insists on feeding the crew from a single pot, and the sergeant logs the stop so the next patrol through knows to bring flour.

is-kurita.objectives.primary: The plant is the heart of the district and your command's responsibility. It must be standing and carrying its full load when the contract ends. If you have to choose between saving the plant and saving a granary, save the plant: the Dragon can replace grain, but not the plant.
is-kurita.storyElementSeed: A patrol halts at a farmstead where one lamp burns; no one speaks to the crew, and an old man stands in the doorway until the machines have walked beyond the tree line. The patrol log records: contact, nil.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Leave It Open, Wire It for Sound
resourceGates.lackingText: Without access to the district depot, you have to buy the seismic and acoustic sets commercially at the DropPort exchange: 11,000 C-bills and 8 days of shipping, instead of 6,000 C-bills and 4 days from the depot stores.

phases.name: POSTURE — THE ALMANAC
phases.lead: The defense is built around a published tide table and a population that reports everything. The work of the quiet weeks is sorting the reports: filtering out the false ones without making the valley feel its reports are ignored, and rehearsing the alignment nights until the lance can run them while exhausted — which is how it will be running them.

dataBlock.Tide cycle: 22.4 hours; flats firm for a 3-hour window twice per cycle
dataBlock.Alignment nights: Tide window plus moon-dark: 4 nights in 28 — printed in every civil almanac on the planet
dataBlock.Report load: 5-12 civilian reports per week; 7 in 10 resolve as ferry traffic, salvagers, or grief — and all of them get walked
dataBlock.Standing posture: 1 militia platoon at the plant, 2 walking the granaries on 8-hour rotations, lance split between plant hardstand and the ferry hill

phases.protocol: On alignment nights, the garrison stands to without sirens, because a siren would send the resettlement camps onto the roads within 20 minutes. The codeword WATERLINE on the garrison net means a crossing has been confirmed on the flats: the plant platoon moves to its south-fence positions, all lights stay off, and the camps are left asleep. A false alarm is called off using the same word with CLEAR added, so no post is left standing at the tide with a rifle for no reason.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading an eager population: why 70 percent false reports work as a screen the raiders never had to build themselves, and how to spot a genuine pre-raid warning sign hidden inside all that noise.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — THE CROSSING
phases.lead: Nine kilometers of firm mud, a 3-hour clock, and a switchyard that loses one transformer for every 5 minutes the raiders hold it. The fight is decided by where the lance is positioned when the WATERLINE call comes in, and by which route it takes to reach the fence.

dataBlock.Crossing window: 3 hours 0 minutes from tide-out; raider lead elements at the south fence by T+12:00 if unopposed
dataBlock.Transformer clock: Charges placeable from T+25:00; 1 transformer rigged per 5 minutes of possession; 3 lost drops the plant below district winter load
dataBlock.Recrossing margin: Raiders must turn for the flats by T+55:00 or abandon the route and fight overland
dataBlock.Tide close: T+160:00 — anything still on the flats, theirs or yours, is lost to the water

routes.name: ASH
routes.desc: Paved plant road running straight from the ferry hill to the south fence, 4.0km.
routes.tradeoff: 9 minutes faster than the other route, but it is in full view of the flats the whole way, so the raiders can count your machines as you approach.

routes.name: KILN
routes.desc: Runs behind the ferry hill ridge, skirting the southern edge of the ruins, 5.7km.
routes.tradeoff: Hidden from the flats until the last 600 meters, but it passes close to the ruins, where salvage-fire heat clutters your sensors and hidden civilian parties may be present. Moving faster than a cruise makes both problems worse.

sidebarKernel.kernel: What a switchyard actually loses with each transformer: the order in which power is shed, which districts go dark first, and why the third transformer is the one you cannot afford to lose.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — LOW WATER
phases.lead: The same tide that carried the raid in also leaves evidence behind. At the next low tide, the flats hold tracks, fluid trails, and whatever the raiders dumped to make their crossing window. You collect the bonus objective there, during the 3-hour window, or you lose it to the returning water.

dataBlock.Evidence window: Next tide-out plus 3 hours; tracks and fluid trails legible for 2 windows at most before the mud takes them
dataBlock.Recovery priorities: Abandoned vehicles first (telemetry cores), track-gauge casts second, fuel-spill samples third — the fuel chemistry points at the forward cache
dataBlock.Pursuit ceiling: Do not pursue onto the flats within 90 minutes of the tide turning; the lost scout car already proved why

sidebarKernel.kernel: The camps after a raid night: what the aid station sees in the week following — and why treating the valley's fear is part of holding the valley.

skeleton: garrison must answer two simultaneous raid axes - property on one, people on the other - with one force while a discovered informer poses arrest, turn, or tolerate choices that reshape its own warning net
inspiration: U.S. Cavalry dispersed-ranch protection against Comanche raiding on the Llano Estacado, 1870s
title: OPERATION LONG FENCE
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} outback, {YEAR}. The contract says 'garrison and protection of district assets,' which out here means a water-cracking plant, six grain silos at the railhead, and 9,000 ranchers scattered across a district the size of a small sea. {EMPLOYER} pays on time and inspects twice a year. The threat keeps no schedule at all. Pirates from the periphery have raided this district 3 times in 5 years, taking water-cracking components, ammunition, and vehicles. On the last visit they also took 11 people. That raid was 14 months ago, and nothing newer has come in since. Having no fresh intelligence is part of the problem: you know they will come, but not when or in what strength. The main terrain problem is the pan: 60 kilometers of dead-flat dry lakebed running the whole eastern edge of the district. At night it is a highway — wheeled, hover, or 'Mech, anything can cross it at full speed. By day, between 1000 and 1500, heat shimmer off the pan blurs optical and infrared sensors past 800 meters, and the mirage layer creates phantom contacts that have twice made the ranch radio net cry wolf this season. You cannot picket 60 kilometers with one lance. You can watch the three bore-water stops on the far side, on the theory that pirates running fuel-burning technicals have to stop there to take on water and cool down — or you can bet that they have switched to fusion power and will not stop at all. The contract defines this patrol routine: a 300-kilometer perimeter circuit flown or driven every 48 hours, radio checks with 14 ranch stations twice a day, and one 'Mech on hot standby at the railhead. The local people are unusually frank: the ranchers like you well enough, and at least one of them is paying the dust toll — the old arrangement, a radio call out to the pan whenever anything worth stealing moves. {NPC:intel-source}, who runs the general store and keeps the district's real intelligence files, puts it plainly: the toll-payer is not a traitor, just a man who has worked out how long a lance takes to reach his homestead. Your job is to change that math. The silos fill in 6 weeks, and full silos are exactly what the pan is watching for. Note the contract's fine print, Section 9: losing a district asset to a raid the adjuster judges 'preventable' triggers the negligence clause — and the employer's adjuster, not you, decides what counts as preventable.

objectives.primary: Do not lose or disable any district asset — the water-cracking plant, the railhead silos, or the rolling stock — to a raid during the contract term.
objectives.secondary: Allow zero civilian abductions from the district's homesteads.
objectives.bonus: Pin down the location of the pirates' grounded DropShip or their anchorage at the edge of the pan, using pursuit tracks, a prisoner's statement, or wreckage from a technical.

complications.name: Mirage Layer
complications.text: Between 1000 and 1500, heat shimmer over the pan defeats optics and infrared past 800 meters and creates phantom contacts. Two false alarms this season have already wasted fuel and damaged the radio net's credibility. The pirates know about this window just as well as you do.
complications.mechanicalEffect: In a daytime fight on the pan, all sensor and visual detection beyond 8 hexes is unreliable: roll 1d6 for each new contact, and on 1-2 it is a mirage, not a real unit. The attacker can close to medium range before being positively identified.

complications.name: Heat Discipline
complications.text: Daytime temperatures beside the pan run 8 to 12 degrees above the temperature a 'Mech is designed for. Coolant has to be trucked in, water is rationed, and an overheated machine on the open lakebed has no shade to cool down in.
complications.mechanicalEffect: In a daytime battle on or beside the pan, every 'Mech gains +2 heat for each turn it moves faster than walking speed, and vehicle crews must make fatigue checks after turn 8.

complications.name: The Dust Toll
complications.text: At least one ranch station radios reports of your movements out to the pirates on the pan. Until you identify which one, assume that any defensive position you set up within sight of a homestead is in the pirates' hands within 6 hours.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The attacker starts the engagement already knowing the defender's standby positions, unless the defender moved those positions during darkness within the previous 12 hours.

complications.name: Six Weeks to Full Silos
complications.text: The silos set the clock. A raid is very unlikely while they stand empty, and grows more likely each week as the harvest fills them. The contract does not end when the silos are full — but the point at which you can no longer afford crew fatigue does.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll on the harvest table for raid timing: on 1-3 the raid comes in week 5-6, on 4-5 in week 7-8, and on 6 there is a feint in week 4 followed by the real raid in week 7.

decisionPoints.name: Two Plumes
decisionPoints.context: When the raid comes, the ranch net reports two dust plumes coming off the pan, 40 kilometers apart: one heading for the railhead silos, one for the homestead cluster. You have one lance and two targets, and the adjuster will write a report no matter what you choose.

options.title: Full Lance to the Railhead
advantages: The contract's named assets are defended at full strength
The railhead fight happens on ground you have prepared, with the standby 'Mech already in position
disadvantages: The homestead cluster is left undefended against the second plume
If that second plume is the slaver group, the cost is paid in lost people
options.consequence: The assets hold, but whatever the second plume came for, it takes. Whether you meet the secondary objective depends entirely on whether that plume was a feint.

costs.resource: you gamble the secondary objective: the homestead cluster stands undefended against the second plume
costs.risk: If the second plume is the slaver group, the cost is paid in people taken — and in the pursuit that follows

options.title: Full Lance to the Homestead Cluster
advantages: The homesteads and the people are protected — abduction is what this district fears most
If the silo plume was the feint, you have read the raid correctly and meet its main attack
disadvantages: The silos and plant are held by the militia section alone
Your exposure under the Section 9 negligence clause is at its highest if the railhead burns
options.consequence: The people are protected, but you are gambling the employer's assets. If the railhead is lost, the negligence clause applies no matter why you chose this.

costs.risk: Maximum Section 9 exposure: losing the railhead triggers the negligence clause against the full value of the contract

options.title: Split the Lance
advantages: Both routes are contested, so neither plume gets a free run
You keep your options open: 10 more minutes to watch the plumes before fully committing
disadvantages: Two under-strength elements, each facing an enemy of unknown size
Open ground like the pan favors whoever concentrates their force, and that will not be you
options.consequence: Both fights happen at 2 units against an unknown force. The engagement becomes two delaying actions racing the reaction timeline, rather than one decisive battle.

costs.resource: you give up concentration: two under-strength elements, each against an enemy of unknown weight
costs.risk: Open ground favors whoever concentrates their force — and that will not be you

decisionPoints.name: The Toll-Payer
decisionPoints.context: Week 3: signals triangulation and the storekeeper's ledger now agree on which ranch station is radioing the pan. The man has a wife, two hired hands, and a homestead 80 kilometers from any help. You can arrest him, you can turn him into your own asset, or you can leave him alone and watch him — each is a real option.

options.title: Arrest, Publicly
advantages: The whole toll network goes quiet across the district within a week
The employer's adjuster records it as due diligence on your part
disadvantages: The pirates lose their source and switch to scouting in person — probes along the edge of the pan that you cannot predict by watching radio traffic
The district's radio net turns cooler toward you, and reports drop by half
options.consequence: You trade a known, readable leak for an unknown one. Civilian reporting drops by 50 percent for the rest of the contract.

costs.resource: civilian reporting drops 50 percent for the rest of the contract
costs.risk: You trade the known, readable leak for pan-edge scouting that no radio-traffic analysis can predict

options.title: Turn Him
advantages: A controlled channel you can use to feed the pirates false information about your positions
His problem is now solved in your favor: protection in exchange for cooperation
disadvantages: A source you have turned can be turned again; the pirates have a longer hold on him than you do
If the employer's adjuster ever finds out you knowingly left a leak in place, the negligence clause applies retroactively
options.consequence: The raid comes in against false positions — the attacker deploys against ground you have already left — unless his loyalty roll fails, in which case the raid comes in against your real positions, now confirmed.

costs.resource: you commit to protecting him: the patrol circuit grows by 160 kilometers each cycle to cover his homestead
costs.risk: If the adjuster finds out you knowingly left a leak in place, the negligence clause applies retroactively, exposing the full contract value

options.title: Leave Him, Watch Him
advantages: His radio traffic is your best early warning: when his transmissions spike, the pirates are listening and a raid is near
No confrontation, no chilling of the radio net, and no clause exposure yet
disadvantages: Every report he sends out stays accurate
You get warning but cannot deceive: you will know the raid is coming, and the raiders will know exactly where you are
options.consequence: The defender gets 12 extra hours of warning before the raid, but the attacker keeps accurate knowledge of your standing positions. Both sides go into the fight well informed.

costs.resource: signals watch: one comms technician assigned to his frequency for the whole contract
costs.risk: His reports stay accurate — the pirates know your positions, and all you know is that they are listening

entries.event: Alarm: the ranch net or a picket reports dust plumes off the pan, a night crossing, with bearings and count uncertain in the dark.
The standby 'Mech moves out and the rest of the lance mounts up. The plume count becomes clear: two columns, 40 kilometers apart.
Fast pirate units (technicals and hover vehicles) reach the outer homesteads on the homestead-cluster route.
From this point, abduction parties can be inside homestead buildings; every 10 minutes after this means another homestead cleared out.
If unblocked, the pirate 'Mech element reaches the railhead and begins blowing up silos or loading loot.
The pirates start their withdrawal across the pan to beat the dawn light and keep enough time to cross back.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: An intercepting force has to be blocking the homestead-cluster route by T+30:00 or abductions begin, and blocking the railhead route by T+40:00 or the silos burn. Meeting both deadlines with a single lance is the whole problem of this mission, and the night will show whether it can be done.

opforSketch.composition: A pirate band: 4-6 stripped-down light and medium 'Mechs (mixed quality, chronically short on ammunition, 1-2 of them with broken secondary weapons), 6-10 armed technicals and light hover transports, and 1 dedicated abduction party of 12-20 raiders in trucks. Green to Regular quality, brave while they are winning.
opforSketch.behavior: Driven by a loot clock. Maximum noise and speed: grab as much cargo and as many people as possible, then cross back over the pan before dawn. They break off the fight at their first 'Mech loss, or at T+75:00, whichever comes first. They never fight to hold ground — only to keep the road home open.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY ANCHOR
forks.trigger: All assets held, zero abductions, and pursuit evidence recovered.
forks.consequence: Track plots converge on a pan-edge anchorage 190 kilometers northeast where the pirates ground their DropShip between raids — an OBJECTIVE_RAID follow-on with a 10-day window before they relocate.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY SADDLE
forks.trigger: Civilians taken from any homestead.
forks.consequence: The trucks are 6 hours ahead and the DropShip will not lift until loaded. An EXTRACTION_RAID pursuit across the pan, against the clock, with the district listening to every transmission.

forks.name: OPERATION SECTION NINE
forks.trigger: Assets damaged but recoverable, or raid repelled with silo stock losses between 10 and 40 percent.
forks.consequence: The employer's adjuster arrives within 20 days to determine whether the loss was 'preventable.' The hearing is fought with patrol logs, not lasers; the toll-payer decision is Exhibit A either way.

storyElementSeed: The water truck makes its dawn round; the driver leaves two extra cans at the picket post without being asked, waves off the receipt, and the gesture goes in the duty log because out here that is what intelligence looks like.

is-davion.objectives.primary: District assets — plant, silos, rolling stock — intact at term's end. That is the whole mission statement. Everything else in this packet is the how.

phases.name: POSTURE — RIDING THE FENCE
phases.lead: The first weeks buy you two things no contract clause can provide: a routine the district trusts, and a baseline normal that lets you recognize the wrong night when it comes. Fly the circuit, keep the radio checks exactly on time, and watch the bore stops on the far side of the pan — because fuel-burning raiders have to take on water there, unless they have switched to fusion and no longer need to.

dataBlock.Patrol circuit: 300km perimeter every 48 hours; radio checks with 14 ranch stations at 0600 and 1800
dataBlock.Bore stops: 3 watered stops on the pan's far side — 41km, 58km, and 66km from the railhead, all beyond response range
dataBlock.Mirage window: 1000-1500 local: optics and IR break beyond 800m over the pan; phantom contacts have burned the ranch net's credibility twice this season
dataBlock.Silo clock: Full in 6 weeks; raid probability climbs week on week with the grain

phases.protocol: Ranch-net discipline: radio checks at 0600 and 1800, answered by name. One missed check is probably just weather; two missed checks in a row means a patrol rides out to investigate, no exceptions, and either way it is logged. There is a duress code built into the weather talk: any station that mentions rain during the dry months is signaling that it is transmitting at gunpoint, and the correct response is to acknowledge it as if it were normal, with no change in your voice.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The coolant ledger: how much daytime operations on the pan cost in trucked-in water and coolant per 'Mech per week, and which line of the contract is supposed to pay for it — because one of them has to.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — TWO PLUMES
phases.lead: The raid shows up as dust: two columns coming off the pan, 40 kilometers apart, and one lance to answer both. The deadlines are fixed — reach the homestead cluster by T+30:00 or the abductions start, reach the railhead by T+40:00 or the silos burn — and whichever route you take tells whoever is paying the dust toll which target you chose.

dataBlock.Axis HOMESTEAD: Homestead cluster, 34km from the railhead standby position; abduction parties inside buildings from T+30:00, one more homestead swept per 10 minutes after
dataBlock.Axis RAILHEAD: Silos and water-cracking plant; pirate 'Mech element arrives T+40:00 if unblocked
dataBlock.Plume resolution: Bearing and count firm up at T+5:00; composition stays unknown until visual range
dataBlock.Pirate break point: First 'Mech loss, or T+75:00, whichever comes first; they fight only to keep their escape route open, never to hold ground

routes.name: STOCK
routes.desc: Graded ranch road to the homestead cluster, 34km, crossing open range the whole way.
routes.tradeoff: Direct, but above 30kph it raises a dust column visible at 20km, so the pirates on the pan see which target you have committed to the moment you commit.

routes.name: IRON
routes.desc: Hard-surfaced rail service road running along the line to the railhead, 19km.
routes.tradeoff: No dust column, full speed — but it only covers the railhead route. Taking it means choosing the silos, in a way the toll-payer can report before you even arrive.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading a feint with one lance and two plumes: which axis a loot-clock raider actually wants, and what 10 more minutes of observation buys against what it costs at T+30:00.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — THE ADJUSTER'S GROUND
phases.lead: The shooting ends and the second fight begins, this one on paper. Track plots, patrol logs, and the toll-payer file are now your evidence: the Section 9 negligence claim is fought with documentation. And the pirates' escape route, plotted carefully, is the opening of your next contract.

dataBlock.Track-plot window: Pan crossings legible for 48-72 hours before wind-scour; pursuit plots converge on the northeast anchorage at 190km
dataBlock.Section 9 exposure: The adjuster defines preventable; patrol logs, radio-check records, and the dust-toll file are the admissible record
dataBlock.District ledger: Zero abductions is the number the ranchers count; the employer counts silo stock to the ton

sidebarKernel.kernel: What a track plot actually proves: gauge, weight class, and heading — and the gap between what the unit knows and what the adjuster will accept as known.

assetDetails.ref: the toll-payer (ranch station on the pan's western rim)
assetDetails.detail: A wife, two hired hands, and a homestead 80km from any help. He transmits reports of your movements out to the pan on a fixed-key radio set he believes cannot be read. His transmission volume rises 24-48 hours before pirate activity, which makes him the district's best raid warning as long as he keeps transmitting. He has worked out your lance's response times; the only thing that will change his behavior is changing those times in his favor.

Runs the general store and keeps the district's real intelligence in a handwritten ledger — debts, who has left, who bought fuel in bulk. He will open the ledger to help you triangulate the toll-payer, but not let you copy it. Keep the store out of every fire plan and every report: the day the district decides the storekeeper talks to soldiers is the day his ledger goes empty.

skeleton: instructor must choose when to arm a green formation against a school-killing raid while the ammunition sits sealed behind an authority whose false invocation costs the instructor's own name
inspiration: German Volkssturm cadre-training overrun by deep armored thrusts, eastern front 1945
title: OPERATION WHETSTONE
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. {EMPLOYER} has put your command in charge of training the valley reserve battalion: 24 armor vehicles, 8 salvage-grade BattleMechs, and 410 personnel whose average age is 19 and whose only combat experience is from holovids. The training ground is the terrace stair — a 300-meter climb up working rice terraces, where every vehicle has to move along dike-top roads only 4 to 6 meters wide, and a thrown track means a 40-ton machine ends up in someone's flooded paddy. The terraces are the district's food supply and the farmers' inheritance. A breached dike floods the terraces below it in a chain reaction, and the district governor has put a number on it: one ruptured retaining wall drowns a year's crop across the 11 terraces below it. Train with that in mind. The battalion's weaknesses are recorded plainly: only 31 percent of crews are gunnery-qualified, vehicle crews throw tracks at 3 times the normal DCMS rate, and the trainee 'Mech lances have never maneuvered above the third terrace at night. Their one strength is just as plain: no trainee has ever refused an order, and the unit would rather die in place than shame its district. That is exactly the instinct an instructor has to train out of them, because the enemy will use it to get them killed. The schedule gives you {TRAINING_WEEKS} weeks until graduation, but the war does not respect schedules. {NPC:intel-source} of the district intelligence office reports a {TARGET_FACTION} deep-raid pattern in this military district: 2 training formations were hit in the past 16 months, both during their final exercises, both apparently aiming to kill the instructors and break the battalions before they could fully form. That assessment is 26 days old and only moderately confirmed, so treat the pattern as likely but not certain. The logic is grimly efficient: killing one training cadre costs the enemy far less than fighting the trained battalion later. Here are the operational facts you inherit. The battalion's war stock — live ammunition, full coolant, mines — is sealed in the cantonment magazine under the district quartermaster's authority. It can only be released on the governor's order, or on your own written declaration that an attack is imminent — and a false declaration brings formal censure against you. Until then, the trainees carry one-quarter of a combat ammunition load. The cantonment sits at the foot of the stair. The only route for a raiding force trying to stay unseen is up the valley floor and onto the stair itself, where the dike roads will funnel them exactly the way they funnel you. The terraces are your terrain problem, your training ground, and — if the pattern holds — your battlefield.

objectives.primary: Keep the training battalion intact as a fighting formation: the instructors alive, trainee losses under 15 percent, and the battalion's colors and command structure intact through any attack.
objectives.secondary: Graduate the battalion on schedule: get gunnery qualification above 60 percent and complete one night movement above the third terrace.
objectives.bonus: Defeat the raid in a way the battalion takes part in. A battalion that has fought a real battle graduates worth twice one that has only trained.

complications.name: Sealed Magazine
complications.text: To release the war stock, you need either the governor's order (4 to 6 hours through official channels) or your own written declaration that an attack is imminent. Even once it is released, actually distributing it — breaking the seals, loading ammunition, swapping out the training loads — takes 95 minutes with green crews working flat out. A false declaration means formal censure, with the battalion watching its instructor disgraced.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Until distribution is complete, all trainee units fight at one-quarter ammunition. The 95-minute distribution clock does not start until a release authority (the governor or your declaration) has been satisfied.

complications.name: The Dikes
complications.text: Every retaining wall holds back water and cannot be rebuilt this season. Weapons fire, falls, and 60-ton machines crossing them can all break them. The governor's chain-reaction math — one broken wall floods 11 terraces and a year of food — applies to fire from both sides, but only your side answers to the district for it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any wall-breaking damage caused by your defending units applies an immediate -1 to employer standing per wall, and these stack. The terraces below a breach become deep-mud hexes after 3 turns.

complications.name: They Will Not Run
complications.text: The trainees' discipline is total, but their judgment is only six weeks old. Ordered to hold, they hold long past the point where it makes sense. A trainee unit will not withdraw — even from a hopeless fight — without an explicit order that names the unit and names the line to fall back to.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Trainee units never withdraw on their own. To disengage a trainee unit, an instructor (cadre) unit must spend a command action that turn while in line of sight or radio contact with it.

complications.name: Pump-House Static
complications.text: The irrigation pumps that lift water up the stair put out broadband electrical noise across the valley floor during every irrigation cycle — 4 hours out of every 12. During a cycle, sensor and radio range on the lower terraces drops sharply. The district intelligence file shows that both previous attacks were timed to hit during pump cycles.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During a pump cycle, radio range is cut to 50 percent and no unit can get sensor locks beyond 10 hexes on the lowest 3 terraces. Roll for the raid's arrival: on 1-4 of 1d6, it comes during a pump cycle.

decisionPoints.name: Declaration
decisionPoints.context: Day {RAID_DAY}, 0340: a picket reports a descending drive flare 60 kilometers down the valley, then nothing — pump-cycle static cuts off any confirmation. This could be the attack pattern, or it could be a meteor and a nervous corporal. The governor is asleep 200 kilometers away. The magazine takes 95 minutes to distribute, and your name goes on anything you sign.

options.title: Declare Imminent Attack — Sign It
advantages: The 95-minute distribution clock starts now, giving you the most possible margin before any contact
The battalion sees its instructor put their own rank on the line for the trainees' lives — a lesson they remember long after tonight
disadvantages: If the flare was nothing, the censure is formal, public, and permanent in your file with {EMPLOYER}
Breaking the war-stock seals ends the training schedule whether the raid comes or not
options.consequence: If the raid arrives after T+95:00, the trainees fight with a full ammunition load. If it never comes, your professional standing pays the price.

costs.resource: the war-stock seals are broken: the training schedule ends tonight, raid or no raid
costs.risk: If the flare was a false alarm, the censure is formal, public, and permanent in your file with {EMPLOYER}

options.title: Wake the Governor — Request Release Through Channels
advantages: The censure risk moves to the proper authority instead of resting on you
Even a 4-to-6-hour channel delay is fine if the raid actually lands tomorrow rather than tonight
disadvantages: If the attack comes during that delay, the battalion meets it at one-quarter ammunition
The request itself, logged and time-stamped, is a record that you suspected an attack and waited
options.consequence: The magazine opens at T+240:00 at the earliest. Anything before that is fought on training loads and the instructors' machines.

costs.resource: channel delay: the magazine opens no sooner than T+240:00
costs.risk: An attack during the delay is met by 410 trainees carrying one-quarter ammunition

options.title: Quiet Measures Only
advantages: No declaration, no censure exposure, and no broken schedule if it turns out to be a false alarm
Spreading the trainees out to night positions is part of the training anyway — you can call it a surprise exercise
disadvantages: The magazine stays sealed; if this is the real raid, the ammunition decision has effectively been made for you by the quartermaster
Only the 4 instructor machines carry full loads against whatever comes down the valley
options.consequence: The battalion is in position but not armed. If the attack comes, the instructors fight a delaying action while 410 trainees run their first real dispersal on quarter loads.

costs.resource: the magazine stays sealed: full ammunition loads ride on the 4 instructor machines alone
costs.risk: If this is the real raid, the ammunition decision was made by the quartermaster, not by you

decisionPoints.name: The Battalion's Place
decisionPoints.context: Contact is confirmed: a raiding force on the valley floor, moving toward the stair under pump-cycle static. The battalion is spread out across the middle terraces. They are not ready. But they are also 24 vehicles and 8 'Mechs, and the enemy did not come all this way to spend the night fighting farmers' walls.

options.title: Cadre Forward, Battalion Held Back
advantages: The trained machines fight the open battle, keeping trainee losses to a minimum
A clean command picture, with no green units in the fire plan to keep track of
disadvantages: Just 4 instructor machines against the full raid, on dike roads with no room to maneuver on the flanks
The battalion watches its instructors get ground down, and learns that lesson instead of how to fight
options.consequence: You protect the trainees by spending the instructors. If the instructor line breaks, the raiders reach a battalion that is intact but has no leaders.

costs.resource: you stake the instructor machines: 4 against the raid on dike roads with no flank room
costs.risk: The instructors' losses are the price paid, and every instructor's machine lost teaches the battalion the wrong lesson

options.title: Battalion Fights Its Ground
advantages: 32 gun platforms on ground they have drilled on for six weeks can outweigh the enemy's better quality at the short ranges of the dike roads
Keeps the bonus objective alive: a battalion that holds its own stair graduates having fought a real battle
disadvantages: Green crews, quarter ammunition loads (unless the magazine was opened), and the no-retreat instinct, on a battlefield with a 300-meter drop
Trainee losses count against the 15 percent ceiling in the primary objective
options.consequence: The raid runs into massed but inaccurate fire from prepared positions. Trainee casualties are decided by the engagement dice, and every dike wall in the fire plan is at risk from fire on both sides.

costs.resource: the governor's math enters the fire plan: one breached wall drowns 11 terraces and costs -1 standing
costs.risk: Trainee casualties are decided by the engagement dice, counting against the 15 percent primary-objective ceiling

options.title: Trade the Stair
advantages: Pulling the battalion and instructors back up the terraces makes the raiders fight uphill against the clock they brought with them
Every terrace you give up buys 20 more minutes for the magazine to open or the governor's column to arrive
disadvantages: Giving up terraces means giving up the farmers' walls and the cantonment below
Withdrawing under pressure is the hardest maneuver there is, and the battalion has never practiced it
options.consequence: The battle becomes a fighting withdrawal up the stair. You gain time, but the raiders gain the cantonment and the lower terraces, and the battalion's discipline is tested at exactly the skill it is worst at.

costs.resource: you give up ground: the cantonment and every lower dike wall go to the raiders while time goes to you
costs.risk: A fighting withdrawal is the battalion's weakest skill, and it will be tested for real

entries.event: Alarm: a picket reports a descending flare 60 kilometers down the valley; pump-cycle static blocks any confirmation.
Instructor machines are crewed and moving, and the battalion recall is sounded across the middle terraces.
Magazine distribution finishes IF the declaration was signed at T+0:00. The trainees have a full ammunition load from this point on, and not a moment before.
The raider column is confirmed on the valley floor, moving toward the foot of the stair under the static.
The raiders reach the cantonment and the lowest dike roads of the stair. By now the battalion is either armed and in position, or it is neither.
Earliest the governor's regular column can arrive from the district capital, 200 kilometers away, if it was summoned at T+0:00.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The battalion has to be armed and in position by T+3:40, when the raiders reach the foot of the stair. A magazine clock started any later than T+2:05 cannot meet that deadline, and the governor's column cannot arrive before T+6:00 no matter when it is called.

opforSketch.composition: A deep-raid force: one Veteran 'Mech lance (a medium-heavy mix, 50-70 tons, with at least 2 machines jump-capable) plus one supporting fast lance (lights, Regular), and no armor or infantry. Built for speed over mass, and for killing instructors rather than taking ground.
opforSketch.behavior: Aims to decapitate. Find and destroy the instructor machines and the command element, wreck the magazine and motor park, avoid the trainee formations except to scatter them, and lift off within 4 hours of landing. Breaks off any fight that costs them time, and presses any fight that turns up instructors.

forks.name: OPERATION FIRST BLADE
forks.trigger: Raid repelled with cadre intact, trainee losses under 15 percent, and the battalion engaged as a formation.
forks.consequence: The battalion graduates blooded and the district governor petitions {EMPLOYER} to send instructor and students together against the raiders' lift point — an OBJECTIVE_RAID with your graduates as the second wave.

forks.name: OPERATION HOLLOW SHEATH
forks.trigger: Cadre machines destroyed or trainee losses exceed 15 percent; battalion combat-ineffective.
forks.consequence: The district loses its forming battalion and knows it; {TARGET_FACTION} returns within 60 days against a province defended by what remains, and your command holds the line through GARRISON_DUTY while a board of inquiry sits in the next room.

forks.name: OPERATION PAPER SEAL
forks.trigger: Battalion preserved but graduation objectives failed, or the magazine declaration proven false.
forks.consequence: The censure process runs its course while training restarts from week one under ISF observation; the next raid window opens before the new graduation date, and everyone involved knows it.

storyElementSeed: Before dawn the trainees rake the vehicle park gravel into straight lines; the instructor walks the lines without a word, and by the time the engines start the rake marks are gone. The task is pointless on purpose: doing a small thing perfectly is the habit that keeps them alive later.

merc.objectives.primary: The contract pays for a trained battalion delivered intact: instructors alive, trainee losses under 15 percent. Dead students mean you failed to deliver what was contracted; dead instructors mean you lost your own people. Keep both numbers at zero wherever you can.
merc.storyElementSeed: Before dawn the trainees rake the vehicle park gravel into straight lines; the contract says nothing about gravel, and the instructor lets them keep the one drill they invented themselves.

phases.name: SYLLABUS — THE STAIR AS SCHOOLHOUSE
phases.lead: The terraces teach what the manuals cannot. A 40-ton machine on a 5-meter dike crown either learns precision or ends up in the water. The training weeks are spent making movement on the stair second nature — because the intelligence file says the final test will come without warning, with live ammunition, from the valley floor.

dataBlock.Battalion at start: 24 armor vehicles, 8 salvage-grade 'Mechs, 410 personnel; gunnery qualified 31 percent; track-throw rate 3 times DCMS standard
dataBlock.Dike roads: 4-6m wide, single file in the bad stretches; one ruptured retaining wall drowns 11 terraces below it
dataBlock.Magazine arithmetic: Training loads one-quarter ammunition; war-stock distribution 95 minutes from a satisfied release authority; governor's channel 4-6 hours
dataBlock.Pump cycles: 4 hours in every 12: communications halved, no sensor locks beyond 10 hexes on the lowest 3 terraces

phases.protocol: During pump cycles, orders go by field telephone and signal lamp, practiced until the battalion is comfortable with them: telephone lines are laid along the dike crowns to each company position, and the cantonment tower lamp signals white for assemble, red for disperse upslope, green for stand fast. Every trainee learns the lamp before the radio. The district file says the enemy attacks during a pump cycle, and the training assumes the file is correct.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Why green crews throw tracks at 3 times the normal rate on dike roads — it is the turn geometry on a 5-meter crown — and the drill that cuts that rate in half in 3 weeks.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — THE EXAMINATION
phases.lead: A descending flare, a pump cycle, and a 95-minute magazine clock against a T+3:40 arrival: the night comes down to whether the declaration was signed in time, and whether the battalion fights on the stair it has trained for. The raiders are coming for the instructors. Where the battalion fits into the fight is the second decision, and the harder one.

dataBlock.Arming deadline: Battalion armed and dispersed by T+3:40 or it is neither; a magazine clock started after T+2:05 cannot meet it
dataBlock.Cadre line: 4 machines at full load regardless; the raiders' doctrine finds instructors and presses
dataBlock.Relief: Governor's column from 200km arrives T+6:00 at the earliest, and only if summoned at T+0:00
dataBlock.Raid economics: The enemy lifts within 4 hours of landing; every terrace traded is 20 minutes purchased

routes.name: AXIS HOE
routes.desc: The western dike line, past the pump stations; its walls are rated for 60 tons and it has the widest crowns on the stair.
routes.tradeoff: Carries the heaviest machines safely, but it runs through the pump-house static: during a cycle, units on HOE can only coordinate by signal lamp and field telephone.

routes.name: AXIS SICKLE
routes.desc: The eastern dike line: older walls, a 40-ton weight limit, hidden from valley-floor observation by the terrace shoulders.
routes.tradeoff: A concealed approach with clean radio, but a single wall failing under a heavy machine floods 11 terraces and costs -1 standing — before the enemy has even fired a shot.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The withdrawal order a trainee unit can actually execute: naming the unit, naming the fallback line, and why an order missing either is an order to die in place.

phases.name: ACCOUNTING — GRADUATION OR INQUIRY
phases.lead: Dawn finds the stair still holding its water, or holding wreckage, and either way the paperwork begins: the dike damage is surveyed against the governor's cost figures, your declaration is reviewed against what actually came down the valley, and the battalion is measured against the only standard that matters — whether it is still a battalion.

dataBlock.Dike survey: Every wall in the fire plan walked within 24 hours; breach count reported to the governor's office with names of the firing units, both sides
dataBlock.Censure clock: A declaration unsupported by an actual raid goes to formal review within 10 days
dataBlock.Graduation ledger: Trainee losses against the 15 percent ceiling; gunnery requalification within 30 days of the engagement counts toward the 60 percent standard

sidebarKernel.kernel: What 95 minutes of distribution actually moved: tonnage of ammunition by vehicle and 'Mech, and the reload arithmetic if the enemy comes back before the magazine is resealed.

assetDetails.detail: He holds the war-stock seals and follows the release order exactly as written, with no interpretation: a written declaration starts the 95-minute clock, while a verbal order is politely refused and logged. He is not an obstacle — he is the system doing its job. An officer who plans around his strictness, rather than fighting it, gains 20 minutes on the night it matters.

He has the trainees' complete trust, and he also embodies their flaw: ordered to hold, he holds past the point of sense, and the battalion holds with him. Any fallback plan that does not keep an instructor within radio or visual range of his position is a plan to lose him and everyone watching him.

3 of the 8 have actuator faults that limit them to walking speed on any slope steeper than 10 degrees. Posted on the lowest terraces, they work fine as gun platforms; ordered upslope under pressure, they become roadblocks on a 5-meter dike crown, with the rest of the battalion stuck behind them.

skeleton: instructor must decide whether to stake its own uninsured machines on its best students while a raid rides a forecast blackout toward the lifeline the school exists to guard
inspiration: Finnish home-guard training under the polar-night Lapland raids, Continuation War 1943-44
title: OPERATION NIGHT SCHOOL
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} border, {YEAR}. The contract is cadre duty: you have 26 weeks to turn the {WORLD} Home Guard — 380 miners, smelter hands, and two genuine veterans — into a force that can make periphery raiders decide this world is not worth the trouble. {EMPLOYER} pays through a provincial development office, and the mining consortium that lobbied for the contract shows up uninvited to your training reviews and takes notes. The trainees are not the problem. They are punctual, tough, and they learn fast, partly because half of them remember the last raid: 4 years ago, the raiders took 2 loads of refined ore and killed 6 Guard in vehicles that should have been scrapped a decade earlier. What you know about the raiders' current strength is 5 months old and mostly rumor, because nothing else crosses this border. Plan for a stronger enemy than the old reports show. The equipment is the problem: 12 armor vehicles split among 3 training companies, average hull age 61 years, and a spare-parts supply that arrives on the consortium's freight schedule, not yours. The key terrain is the moraine: a boulder belt 2 kilometers wide and 30 long, the only ground between the icefield and the fjord that will carry armor or 'Mechs in any season. Anyone coming for the town, the smelter, or the geothermal plant has to come through the moraine — there is no other route — and the defenders have to use it too, single file in the worst stretches, with house-sized boulders blocking every line of sight at 100 to 300 meters. The weather sets the schedule: high-latitude auroral storms black out radio and degrade sensors across the whole planet for 30 to 70 hours at a time. They can be forecast 2 days ahead, and the raid 4 years ago came in the third hour of one. The local night lasts 40 hours out of every 56, so the Guard trains in the dark because the fighting will be in the dark. You will get to know the waiting: storm forecasts pinned up by the mess hatch, the geothermal plant's steam plume standing straight up on still nights — visible 30 kilometers away, effectively the town's own beacon — and the consortium's ore tonnage reports telling anyone with a radio exactly when the warehouses are worth robbing. {NPC:employer-contact} forwards those reports to your operations tent with a standing apology. The Guard has to be ready before the warehouses fill. The contract says 26 weeks; the ore says week {RAID_WEEK}.

objectives.primary: Get the {WORLD} Home Guard to certified readiness — 60 percent gunnery qualification and one full-company night exercise completed in the moraine — and keep it intact as an organized formation through any raid during the training term.
objectives.secondary: Keep raid damage to the geothermal plant, smelter, and ore warehouses under 10 days' repair.
objectives.bonus: Destroy enough of the raiders' equipment to end raids for the season — counted as 2 or more 'Mechs, or half their vehicles.

complications.name: Auroral Blackout
complications.text: Storm forecasts give 2 days' warning of radio and sensor blackouts lasting 30 to 70 hours. The raiders attack during these storms. Inside one, there is no long-range warning network, no air picture, and no way to call the DropPort. You are back to runners, telephone wire, and signal flares, like an army of the previous century.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During storm turns, no unit can use sensors beyond 6 hexes, and units more than 10 hexes apart cannot coordinate by radio. Command actions require line of sight, a flare, or a wire connection.

complications.name: Twelve Hulls, Three Companies
complications.text: The Guard's 12 vehicles rotate among the companies on a published training schedule. At any alarm, two-thirds of the trained crews have no vehicle, and the vehicles are wherever the schedule put them, crewed by whichever company drew them that week.
complications.mechanicalEffect: At the start of the raid, roll 1d6. On 1-2 the vehicles are at the moraine range (well-positioned); on 3-4 they are in the town motor park (20 minutes from their positions); on 5-6 they are split between both with mixed crews, and each vehicle activates on a 4+ during the first 3 turns.

complications.name: The Plume
complications.text: On still nights, the geothermal plant's steam plume marks the town's location from 30 kilometers away. Shutting the plant down hides that marker, but it also cuts heat and power to 4,000 people during a subarctic night that lasts 40 hours. The town council will not vote to freeze on the chance that a raid might come.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The attacker always knows the bearing to the town and approaches with no navigation error, unless the defender wins a council vote (one attempt, before the storm) to run the plant at quarter load. If that vote passes, the cold imposes a -1 on all defending infantry effectiveness after turn 10.

decisionPoints.name: Whose Machines
decisionPoints.context: Week {RAID_WEEK}, storm forecast posted: a 60-hour blackout is inbound, and the warehouses are full. Your unit's spare and workshop 'Mechs — the ones not on your own roster sheets — could put your 4 best trainee crews into real machines for the storm. But the contract's Annex C is explicit: damage trainees cause to your unit's property is not reimbursed. The trainees know the machines exist; they have been polishing them, unasked, for a month.

options.title: Lend the Spares
advantages: 4 more 'Mechs on the line, crewed by trainees who have earned them
The Guard fights its own defense, which gives the readiness certification real meaning afterward
disadvantages: Every hit to a lent machine is a loss your unit eats, uncompensated, under Annex C
A trainee killed while flying your colors is a different kind of cost, and the town will hold you to it
options.consequence: The defender adds 4 trainee-crewed 'Mechs (Green pilots, your machines). All damage to them is paid out of unit funds after the mission.

costs.resource: you commit 4 workshop 'Mechs from off your own roster sheets
costs.risk: Under Annex C, all damage to lent machines is uncompensated — armor repair alone runs 8,000 to 12,000 C-bills per machine that fights

options.title: Your Pilots in Every Cockpit
advantages: Maximum combat performance from every available machine
No Annex C exposure, and no trainee in a cockpit they have only 9 simulator hours toward flying
disadvantages: Your own techs and reserve pilots fight while trained Guard crews stand in a trench and watch
The certification review will note that the Guard's own machines were not trusted to the Guard
options.consequence: The defender fields full professional crews. Keeping the Guard in a supporting role costs 10 percent off the readiness certification score, regardless of how the fight goes.

costs.resource: readiness certification: -10 percent regardless of outcome
costs.risk: Your techs and reserve pilots are on the line, and casualties among them are your own losses, not a failure to deliver the contract

options.title: Spares Stay Cold — Guard Fights Its Own Equipment
advantages: A clean contract position: no lending, no Annex C, no mixed crews
The 12 vehicles and the trench lines are the honest measure of 26 weeks of training
disadvantages: Four good machines sit in a shed during the very fight they were polished for
