If the line breaks for lack of armor, everyone will know where that armor was
options.consequence: The defense is fought with the Guard's actual order of battle. The result, good or bad, is credited to the training itself — and so is the after-action report.

costs.risk: No Annex C exposure and no extra machines; if the line breaks for lack of armor, the after-action report names the shed those machines sat in

entries.event: Alarm: the fjord-mouth watch post fires a red flare — hulls on the water, count unknown, in the third hour of the auroral storm.
Runners reach the motor park and the trench line; vehicle crews head to wherever the schedule left their machines.
The Guard's blocking companies need to be moving into the moraine positions now — the worst stretches take 20 minutes to occupy in the dark.
If unopposed, the raiders' lead units clear the moraine's north mouth and have open ground to the plant intake and warehouses.
From this point, the raiders can finish loading at the warehouses; every further 15 minutes means one more load of ore lost.
Storm or no storm, the raiders begin their withdrawal to beat the Guard's only mobile reserve, which is coming around the flank of the icefield.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The moraine blocking positions must be manned by T+0:35. If the raiders clear the north mouth unopposed at T+0:50, they reach the plant intake — and a damaged intake means 40 hours of subarctic night with no heat for 4,000 people.

opforSketch.composition: A periphery raiding company: 3-5 'Mechs (worn mediums, plus one heavy if the season has gone well), 4-8 tracked and hover vehicles fitted for hauling cargo, and 1-2 platoons of raider infantry in powered cargo exoskeletons that double as assault troops. Regular quality, and they know the moraine intimately.
opforSketch.behavior: Commercial raiders: cargo matters more than kills. They engage only what stands between their column and the warehouses, and slip past resistance through side channels in the moraine where a single 'Mech can just squeeze. They withdraw on schedule at T+3:00, or the instant they lose any 'Mech, because those machines are their capital for next season.

forks.name: OPERATION PAID SEASON
forks.trigger: Raid repelled with raider materiel losses at bonus threshold, Guard intact and certified.
forks.consequence: The consortium, suddenly generous, funds a punitive option: a PIRATE_HUNTING follow-on tracing the raiders' withdrawal to a depot moon two jumps out, with the certified Guard taking over home defense behind you.

forks.name: OPERATION EMBER TITHE
forks.trigger: Plant intake hit or Guard broken as a formation.
forks.consequence: The town goes onto emergency heat rationing through the storm season and the consortium invokes the contract's performance review. Your command escorts heat-exchanger freight up from the DropPort through ambush country — RELIEF_DUTY with the town watching every convoy.

forks.name: OPERATION RANSOM CLASS
forks.trigger: Raid repelled but raiders extracted with prisoners or a lent unit machine.
forks.consequence: A ransom note arrives via tramp freighter 3 weeks later, priced in ore. The consortium will not pay, the families cannot, and the EXTRACTION_RAID option has a 1-jump-window expiry date.

storyElementSeed: The wind has closed the gunnery range again, so the class meets in the equipment shed: chalk firing solutions on the back of a blast door, attendance voluntary, every seat full.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: The Home Guard readiness certification is a deliverable under provincial development grant 7-114-C, audited at the end of the term: 60 percent gunnery qualification, one company-strength night exercise completed, formation intact. The audit requires the consortium's co-signature, and the consortium reads the drafts. Plan the paperwork as carefully as you plan the trench lines.

resourceGates.lackingText: Your unit funds cannot cover the Annex C repair exposure on 4 lent machines, so the spares stay in the shed. Lending out armor you cannot afford to repair means you only get to lend it once.

phases.name: TERM — TEACHING THE DARK
phases.lead: You have 26 weeks, but the ore calendar may not give you all of them. The training term builds the Guard around the moraine and the storm drill — wire, flares, runners — because the raid 4 years ago came in the third hour of a blackout, and nobody on {WORLD} assumes the next one will be any gentler.

dataBlock.Guard at start: 380 personnel, 2 veterans, 12 armor vehicles across 3 companies, average hull age 61 years
dataBlock.Local night: 40 hours of every 56; all gunnery and movement training scheduled into it deliberately
dataBlock.Storm forecasting: 2 days' warning of 30-70-hour blackouts; raids ride the storms
dataBlock.Wire net: Field telephone lines from fjord-mouth watch post to motor park and trench line — laid by week 6, walked weekly thereafter

phases.protocol: Storm-condition signal plan, practiced monthly: a red flare from the fjord-mouth post means hulls on the water, count unknown — every station acts on it without waiting for confirmation. Green means general recall; white means the position is compromised, fall back to the trench line. Runners carry written copies of every flare order, because the moraine blocks radio even on clear days, and inside a storm the flare and the telephone wire are your entire command network.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Keeping 61-year-old vehicles running on the consortium's parts schedule: which order to cannibalize them in, and which 2 of the 12 are the parts donors nobody mentions at parade.

phases.name: STORM WATCH — THE SIXTY HOURS
phases.lead: Forecast posted, warehouses full, blackout inbound: the Guard goes onto storm footing, and the question of whose machines stand the line has to be answered before the weather closes in. Whatever you decided, the moraine is the battlefield — there is no other route, for them or for you.

dataBlock.Blocking deadline: Moraine positions manned by T+0:35; the bad stretches take 20 minutes to occupy in the dark
dataBlock.North mouth: Raiders clearing it unopposed at T+0:50 have open running to plant intake and warehouses
dataBlock.Loss meter: Loading complete from T+1:30; one ore lift lost per 15 minutes after
dataBlock.Raider withdrawal: At T+3:00, or the loss of any 'Mech; the machines are their capital for next season, and they protect them accordingly

routes.name: CAIRN
routes.desc: The main freight cut through the moraine, 11m wide and graded — the route the ore trucks use, and the one the raiders used 4 years ago.
routes.tradeoff: Fast for both sides. A blocking position here meets the raid head-on, at boulder-broken sightlines of 100-300m, and either holds or is overrun.

routes.name: SKERRY
routes.desc: A side channel threading the eastern edge of the boulder belt — wide enough for only one 'Mech at 3 points, exiting behind the warehouse row.
routes.tradeoff: A concealed approach for a flanking force or a raider bypass. Whoever holds its exit controls the back door to the warehouses, and whoever gets caught in its narrow points fights one machine at a time.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Fighting a raid that wants tonnage, not kills: where a defense thins itself by guarding everything, and the one position the raiders cannot route around.

phases.name: CERTIFICATION — THE AUDIT
phases.lead: The storm passes and the term is graded: the Guard against its readiness standard, the equipment accounts against Annex C, and the season against the bonus target — 2 raider 'Mechs or half their vehicles, the price of a year's quiet. The consortium shows up uninvited, taking notes.

dataBlock.Certification standard: 60 percent gunnery qualification, one full-company night exercise in the moraine, formation intact
dataBlock.Annex C ledger: Trainee-caused damage to unit property non-compensable; armor repair on a lent machine that fought runs 8,000-12,000 C-bills
dataBlock.Season arithmetic: Raider losses at 2 'Mechs or half their vehicle strength prices {WORLD} out of next season's circuit

sidebarKernel.kernel: What the readiness certificate is actually worth: the consortium's insurance premium drops, the development office's grant renews, and neither number appears in the unit's contract — leverage for the next negotiation, if anyone writes it down.

assetDetails.detail: Both former line soldiers, and the Guard's only real combat experience. One teaches gunnery and qualifies crews at twice the normal rate; the other has not set foot in a 'Mech bay since his discharge and will not say why. Put the first on the line and the second on the trench line, and do not swap them just to make a point — the Guard watches both men every day and takes its nerve from them.

9 simulator hours each toward your workshop machines. They are the best in the program at night gunnery and the worst at heat discipline — and the lent spares run hot. If you lend them the machines, write the standing order on the cockpit glass: alpha strikes are for the simulator only.

Forwards the consortium's ore tonnage reports with a standing apology, and has no power to stop them. He can delay publishing one report by 10 days, once per term, if asked in writing — 10 days of the warehouses looking emptier than they are, to be spent wisely or wasted.

skeleton: security force must hunt infiltrators living beneath its own facility while the final assault arrives as three simultaneous attacks of which the reserve can answer only one
inspiration: Soviet defence of the Stalingrad tractor works against sewer-borne infiltration, 1942
title: OPERATION STILL FORGE
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The weapons complex runs around the clock, so its guard does too. {EMPLOYER} has assigned your command to plant security for one production quarter: 9,000 workers across 3 shifts, a 22-kilometer perimeter, a rail spur that receives or sends out a train every 6 hours, and at the center of it all, Line Three — the only assault-class gantry line on the planet, currently {BATCH_SIZE} machines short of finishing a production batch that {TARGET_FACTION} would rather destroy than let march. The plant has been raided before, and the corridor war guarantees it will be raided again. The files cannot tell you when, and the waiting is the job. Your terrain problem is underneath your feet: the Number Four slag channel and its 5 sister channels, decommissioned cooling canals from the plant's pre-Exodus expansion, running 30 kilometers under and through the industrial belt at 4 to 9 meters below ground level. They are mapped, gated, and grated — but the gratings are 80 years old, the maps contradict each other in 14 places, and a fire team moving down there is invisible to every sensor on the wall. The second problem is heat: thermal pollution from the foundry makes infrared useless inside the industrial belt — a BattleMech at 200 meters reads as just another slag pour. Security here comes down to eyes, badges, and routine: the gates cycle at shift change three times a day, when 3,000 workers squeeze through 4 gates over 40 minutes and the line stretches 400 meters in any weather; trains are inspected on boarding against manifests that the dispatcher's office amends by hand; and the ISF resident's office countersigns — or refuses — every security measure that touches production. Be clear on the command arrangement: you can stop anything you want, but halting Line Three without ISF agreement is a production failure with your name on it, and production failures on {WORLD} are answered for in court. {NPC:intel-source} reads the threat as having two layers, and this read is only 6 days old and well confirmed. First, a {TARGET_FACTION} commando element of 2 to 3 teams is already on-world under cover as drafted laborers, tasked to destroy Line Three's gantry controls. Second, a raid lance waits somewhere outside the pattern — aboard a freighter, or already scattered in the agricultural belt — ready to hit the perimeter when the commandos call for it. The batch is finished in 19 days. Acceptance trials and rail dispatch follow within 72 hours of that. Every day closer to dispatch, the target is worth more and the strike is more certain.

objectives.primary: Keep damage to Line Three and its gantry controls under 30 days' repair, and get the production batch onto its train and out.
objectives.secondary: Hold the perimeter: no hostile force crosses the wall or the channels without being detected and engaged.
objectives.bonus: Take at least one commando alive for the ISF resident. The network behind the labor-draft covers is worth more than the raid itself.

complications.name: Below Grade
complications.text: Six decommissioned slag channels run under the complex at 4 to 9 meters below ground level. The gratings are corroded, the channel maps contradict each other in 14 places, and nothing down there shows up on the wall sensors. Walking one channel takes a squad 11 hours, and you do not have enough squads or enough hours to walk them all.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Attacker infantry may use hidden movement to deploy to any below-grade map point, unless the defender has swept that specific channel within the previous 48 hours. The defender sweeps 1 channel per 11 squad-hours spent.

complications.name: Foundry Bloom
complications.text: Thermal pollution across the industrial belt blinds infrared sensors. A shut-down 'Mech in a slag yard, a hot APC behind a casting shed — all of it reads as ordinary process heat. The wall's infrared arrays were calibrated too optimistically by a contractor who has been dead for 40 years.
complications.mechanicalEffect: No infrared detection works inside the industrial belt — visual and seismic only. Shut-down or low-power units cannot be detected beyond visual range anywhere on the plant map.

complications.name: Shift Change
complications.text: Three times a day, 3,000 workers squeeze through 4 gates over 40 minutes. At that volume, the badge readers fail at a documented 2 percent rate; checking badges by hand doubles the queue, and the length of the queue sets the city's mood. Both raids on this plant in living memory came during a shift-change window.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During a shift-change window, reaction moves from the gate sections are delayed by 2 turns. Roll for the raid's H-hour: on 1-4 of 1d6, it falls inside a window.

complications.name: Countersignature
complications.text: Any measure that stops or slows Line Three — a lockdown, flooding the channels, isolating the power — needs ISF agreement, which takes 2 to 5 hours and comes back as a question about why you needed it. The resident is not hostile, just careful, and careful is slow.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Defensive measures that affect production take effect 2-5 hours (roll 1d4+1) after the defender orders them — unless ordered after the first shots are fired, in which case they take effect immediately.

decisionPoints.name: The Channels Question
decisionPoints.context: Day 11 of 19. A grating in the Number Four slag channel is found cut and then re-wired to look intact — careful handiwork, not corrosion. The commandos are below grade now, or have been. You can flood the channels from the river intake (with ISF agreement), sweep them squad by squad, or leave the cut grating in place and watch it.

options.title: Flood the Channels
advantages: Shuts down the entire below-grade network in 3 hours — no infiltration route survives
No friendly casualties in 30 kilometers of dark tunnels
disadvantages: Needs ISF countersignature: 2 to 5 hours of exposure between giving the order and the water arriving
The works engineer warns that floodwater undercuts Line Three's foundations: an 8 percent chance of subsidence damage that you, not the raiders, will have caused
options.consequence: The infiltration route closes, but the commandos surface early and switch to their fallback plan, and the raid's H-hour moves earlier — sooner, with less preparation on both sides.

costs.resource: ISF countersignature: 2 to 5 hours with the route still open, between the order and the water
costs.risk: An 8 percent chance of subsidence at Line Three — production damage you ordered and have to answer for

options.title: Sweep Number Four, Squad by Squad
advantages: Confirms the channel is clear, with a chance at the bonus objective — a live commando taken below grade
No effect on production, no countersignature needed, no engineer's warning
disadvantages: 11 hours of squad time spent on one channel while 5 others go unwatched
A fight below grade is grenades at 10 meters, and your infantry pays the price to get in
options.consequence: Number Four is cleared or contested within a day, but the other channels stay open to the attacker, and your infantry is tied up below grade just when the wall needs it.

costs.resource: 11 squad-hours below grade while 5 channels go unwatched
costs.risk: A below-grade fight is grenades at 10 meters, and your infantry pays the price to get in

options.title: Watch the Cut Grating
advantages: The known entrance becomes your sensor: anyone who uses it is seen without realizing it
Full squad strength stays on the wall and the gates
disadvantages: The maps disagree in 14 places, so the cut grating may be only one entrance of three
Watching means letting the approach happen — the fight begins on the attacker's timing, not yours
options.consequence: The defender automatically detects any force using Number Four, but gets no warning at all from the channels nobody is watching.

costs.resource: one squad tied to watching Number Four around the clock
costs.risk: The maps disagree in 14 places — the entrance you are watching may be only one of three

decisionPoints.name: Junction, Spur, or Line
decisionPoints.context: H-hour: demolition alarms at Line Three, weapons fire at the rail spur where the train is loading, and the wall reporting 'Mech-weight contacts at the agricultural fence. The reserve lance can hold one fight in time and reinforce a second one late. The third fight is the militia's alone.

options.title: Reserve to Line Three
advantages: The primary objective gets the lance — the gantry line is what this whole quarter is about
Demolition teams die fastest once 'Mechs arrive, so the 25-minute rigging clock can be beaten
disadvantages: The loaded train on the spur is the most easily-stolen prize on the plant map
The wall contacts move into the belt unchallenged, wherever they are actually headed
options.consequence: The gantry is defended at full strength, but the batch on the spur survives only if the militia's spur platoon holds longer than its training suggests it will.

costs.risk: The loaded train holds only as long as the militia spur platoon does — expected to break around T+6:00

options.title: Reserve to the Rail Spur
advantages: The finished machines are saved; losing them would be a total, unrecoverable loss
The spur is open ground, where 'Mech firepower has clear lanes it does not have among the casting sheds
disadvantages: Line Three's defense comes down to gate guards against demolition specialists who only need 25 minutes
If the spur fight was the feint, you have committed your force to defending the diversion
options.consequence: The batch is defended where it sits, but Line Three's survival depends on whether the alarms there were the real strike or just noise.

costs.risk: Line Three left to face demolition specialists on a 25-minute clock; a wired-to-blow gantry takes years to replace, not one quarter

options.title: Hold the Reserve at the Junction
advantages: Keeping the force uncommitted lets it respond to whichever fight turns out to be real — 6 minutes to the spur, 9 to the line
To draw you in, the attacker has to commit real weight, spending surprise to do it
disadvantages: Both opening fights run on militia strength alone while the lance waits at the crossroads
Both the demolition clock and the loading clock keep running during the 6-to-9-minute reaction lag
options.consequence: The lance reaches the decisive point late but at full strength. Everything before it arrives is paid for by the militia, with militia casualties.

costs.resource: the lance waits at the crossroads while both opening fights run on militia strength alone
costs.risk: Both the demolition clock and the loading clock keep running through the 6-to-9-minute reaction lag

entries.event: Alarm: a demolition charge registers on seismic sensors in the Line Three sub-basement, with small-arms fire at the rail spur gate at the same moment. H-hour is now.
Gate sections report 'Mech-weight movement through the agricultural fence line, count uncertain in the foundry bloom.
The reserve lance reaches the rail spur if it was sent there at T+0:00. The militia spur platoon's expected holding time runs out.
The reserve lance reaches Line Three if it was sent there at T+0:00.
If left uninterrupted from T+0:00, the commando demolition rigging at Line Three is complete — from this point the gantry controls are wired to be destroyed.
If unengaged, the raid lance finishes its run through the belt and reaches the spur or the line — whichever one the commandos have opened up.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Line Three's sub-basement has to be cleared of demolition teams before the rigging is complete at T+25:00. Once the gantry is wired, it is lost whether or not the trigger team survives, and replacing the line takes years.

opforSketch.composition: A two-layer force. Inside: 2-3 commando teams of 5-6 specialists each (Veteran/Elite), tasked with demolition, carrying satchel charges, suppressed weapons, and plant coveralls. Outside: one fast raid lance (Regular/Veteran mediums, 45-60 tons, at least 2 jump-capable), tasked to breach the fence, pin the defense in place, and open a path for the commandos to extract or for the batch to be destroyed.
opforSketch.behavior: The commandos are fanatically committed: they keep rigging charges under fire until the team can no longer function. The raid lance fights for time, not ground — it pushes wherever the defense gets thin, breaks off at 50 percent damage, and abandons the commandos without hesitation if extracting them would cost the lance.

forks.name: OPERATION RETURN POST
forks.trigger: Line Three intact, batch dispatched, and at least one commando taken alive.
forks.consequence: The prisoner's labor-draft cover unravels into a staging point in the agricultural belt — an OBJECTIVE_RAID follow-on against the raid lance's hide site before it lifts off-world, window 6 days.

forks.name: OPERATION SCATTERED ANVIL
forks.trigger: Line Three gantry destroyed or wired beyond 30-day repair.
forks.consequence: Production disperses to three secondary sites pending reconstruction, and your command escorts gantry segments and machine tools by road and rail through a corridor {TARGET_FACTION} now watches with confidence — sustained SECURITY_DUTY at elevated threat, under a cloud.

forks.name: OPERATION QUENCH
forks.trigger: Evidence indicates worker collusion in the infiltration — badges, channel keys, or amended manifests traced inside.
forks.consequence: The ISF resident's investigation moves through the shifts like cold air. Arrest sweeps at the gates, a slowdown on the lines, and your command holding the wall between 9,000 workers and the resident's schedule — RIOT_DUTY in everything but name.

storyElementSeed: At shift change the gate line stretches 400 meters in the rain; a guard checks badges by hand because the reader is down again, and the line waits without complaint, because the line has always waited and the rain has always rained.

merc.objectives.primary: Contract deliverable: Line Three operational, and the production batch loaded on its train at dispatch. The employer's penalty schedule for a lost gantry line has a number in it you should be sitting down to read. The ISF countersignature requirement is in Annex B, and it is not negotiable, even when it should be.

BATCH_SIZE.unit: assault-class BattleMechs in the production batch

phases.name: THE PATTERN — GATES, CONSISTS, SHIFTS
phases.lead: Plant security is about knowing the normal pattern: 19 days of gate cycles, trains, and badge queues, watched closely enough that the one wrong morning stands out. The commandos are already inside that pattern under cover as drafted laborers, learning yours.

dataBlock.Perimeter: 22km of wall; 9,000 workers across 3 shifts; rail consist every 6 hours
dataBlock.Shift change: 3,000 workers through 4 gates over 40 minutes, 3 times daily; badge readers fail at 2 percent under throughput; both prior raids came inside a window
dataBlock.Sensor truth: Foundry bloom blinds IR across the industrial belt — visual and seismic only; a shut-down 'Mech at 200m reads as a slag pour
dataBlock.Countersignature: Production-affecting measures take 2-5 hours through the ISF resident's office — until first shots, when they take effect immediately

phases.protocol: Gate procedure for the quarter: badge failures are checked by hand at a separate lane, never in the main queue — a long queue both sours the city's mood and gives the commandos cover. Send one written contingency plan to the resident's office 48 hours before you need it, because a pre-signed measure is the only fast one available here.

sidebarKernel.kernel: How a labor-draft cover identity is built: which 3 documents a drafted worker carries, which one is hardest to forge, and why the gate is still the wrong place to catch a commando.

phases.name: BELOW GRADE — THE CHANNELS
phases.lead: Day 11's cut grating changes the channels from a mapping problem into an occupied one. Six channels, 30 kilometers, 14 places where the maps disagree: this phase is a race between clearing the channels and H-hour, fought at lamp range in the tunnels right beneath the plant you are defending.

dataBlock.Channel network: 6 decommissioned slag channels, 4-9m below grade, 30km total; nothing below grade registers on wall sensors
dataBlock.Sweep cost: 11 squad-hours per channel; a swept channel stays denied for 48 hours, then reverts
dataBlock.Map conflicts: 14 points where the channel surveys contradict each other — every one a possible unmapped junction
dataBlock.The cut grating: Number Four, craft work re-wired to look whole; one known door of an unknown count

phases.protocol: Below-grade procedure: squads move on telephone-wire reels, not radio — the channels block transmission, and the commandos may be listening anyway. Challenge SLAGFALL, reply CRUCIBLE, changed at each shift bell. Any squad that finds fresh tool marks halts, marks the spot, and withdraws; you cannot plan a fight in these channels until you have actually mapped them.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reading 80-year-old gratings — corrosion versus deliberate cutting: the 4 signs of a cut dressed up to look like decay, and why the works' own maintenance logs have a date for every honest repair.

phases.name: H-HOUR — THREE ALARMS
phases.lead: When it comes, it comes as three fights at once — Line Three, the spur, the wall — set up so the reserve lance can only win one of them in time. The 25-minute rigging clock at the gantry is the number that every other number is built around.

dataBlock.Reserve reach: Junction to spur 6 minutes, junction to Line Three 9 minutes
dataBlock.Rigging clock: Demolition wiring at the gantry complete at T+25:00 if uninterrupted; a wired gantry is a lost gantry
dataBlock.Wall contacts: 'Mech-weight movement through the agricultural fence from T+4:00, count unresolvable in the foundry bloom

sidebarKernel.kernel: Triage among three alarms: which fight is unrecoverable if lost, which is expensive, and which is noise — and the discipline of deciding in 60 seconds with the bloom hiding the count.

phases.name: DISPATCH — THE CONSIST OUT
phases.lead: Surviving the raid is not the mission; getting the batch loaded and out is. The last 72 hours cover acceptance trials, loading, and a rail departure through a corridor the enemy has just shown it can reach. The quarter is won when the train's wheels pass the wall.

dataBlock.Dispatch window: Acceptance trials and rail dispatch within 72 hours of batch completion
dataBlock.Loading rate: 40 minutes per machine onto flatcars with the gantry cranes; the batch is defenseless cargo from first lift to last tie-down
dataBlock.Manifest control: The dispatcher's office amends manifests by hand — the same hands the infiltrators needed

phases.protocol: Dispatch protocol: no train leaves on an amended manifest unless every hand-written change is initialed by the dispatcher with a guard watching; 3 or more changes on a single page holds the train for a full physical inspection against the boarding count. The batch train itself runs sealed, inspected at the wall, with the escort assigned before the engine couples on.

sidebarKernel.kernel: What {BATCH_SIZE} assault machines look like as freight: axle loads, crane cycles, tie-down points — and the 40 minutes per machine when the quarter's entire purpose is hanging from a crane hook.

assetDetails.detail: The control cabinets are original pre-Exodus equipment. You can fit armor plate over the cabinet row in 2 days of line downtime (which the ISF must countersign), but the logic boards inside cannot be obtained any closer than the capital. A fire in that row alone is a 30-day-plus repair — and the commandos know which row it is.

{BATCH_SIZE} assault-class machines, unfueled, unarmed, waiting for acceptance trials — the most valuable objects on the planet, and the most helpless. They cannot defend themselves and cannot be moved without the gantry cranes; their only protection is their position, not weapons.

Careful rather than hostile, and slow by policy. He will pre-sign exactly one contingency measure if it reaches him as a written plan 48 hours ahead — flood, lockdown, or power isolation; choose before day 11. His countersignature on the right document is worth more than a platoon; on the wrong document, it is worth a production inquiry.

skeleton: security force must defend a depot whose sensors go blind on a published industrial schedule while silencing the noise source would destroy the economy and political cover the garrison depends on
inspiration: U.S. defence of the Khe Sanh fuel and ammunition dumps amid karst infiltration ground, 1968
title: OPERATION HOLLOW GROUND
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The asset is the fuel and ordnance depot: 40 hectares of fuel tanks, bunkered munitions, and pumping equipment that keeps the planet's aerospace wing flying. The wing is what makes {TARGET_FACTION} raids on this world expensive, and the depot is what keeps the wing in the air. Burn the depot and the fighters are useless for a whole campaign season — and {TARGET_FACTION}'s planners can do that math as well as ours. {EMPLOYER} wants the depot still standing at the end of the quarter. Everything else in this packet supports that one goal. The terrain problem is right under your boots: the karst, a 7-kilometer belt of limestone sinkhole country wrapping around the depot's southern and eastern approaches. The karst defeats ground-survey maps — {NEW_SINKHOLES} new collapses opened last wet season alone, and the cave system below is mapped to 60 percent at best. The survey is 6 years old and unreliable, so a sinkhole that can hide a fire team today may have been solid ground last quarter. Ground radar sweeps run once a quarter, and the gaps between sweeps are the enemy's working room. The karst also fools your instruments: cave acoustics bend seismic and sound bearings by 15 to 40 degrees, so a footstep heard at post nine may actually be a machine two ridgelines away from where the sensors place it. Here is the routine you take over: a perimeter walked in 4-hour shifts across 14 posts, dog teams on the karst rim at dawn and dusk, ground radar re-surveying 1 sector per week, and a civilian quarry 3 kilometers south that blasts on a published schedule — which conveniently covers the sound of anything else that thumps. The dry season starts during the contract window, and dry season is raid season: hard landing zones everywhere, and every vehicle on the approach roads raising a dust column visible at 20 kilometers, yours included. The wing flies cover patterns it cannot keep up around the clock; there is a 90-minute gap in air cover every cycle while fighters recover and turn around, and that gap drifts through the day on a schedule a patient observer can work out in two weeks of watching. Assume the observer has been watching longer than that. {NPC:intel-source} is sure a {TARGET_FACTION} raid is coming but cannot give a date: lance-to-company strength, fire-mission tactics, the depot as the target. The depot has survived 9 raid seasons. The sergeants who kept it standing will tell you the same thing the karst does: the ground you trust is the ground that swallows you.

objectives.primary: Keep the depot — tank rows, munitions bunkers, pump house — intact through the contract term, with total damage no more than 10 percent of storage capacity.
objectives.secondary: Never interrupt the aerospace wing's sortie schedule with depot security measures for more than one 24-hour period.
objectives.bonus: Recover the raiders' approach maps or pathfinder records. Someone surveyed the karst for them, and {EMPLOYER}'s counterintelligence wants to know who.

complications.name: The Ground Lies
complications.text: There are unmapped voids under the karst belt. Heavy units that leave the surveyed roads risk a collapse — and the survey is 6 years old. Last wet season opened {NEW_SINKHOLES} new sinkholes, and nobody has funded a survey to find out what they connect to.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any unit of 40 tons or more entering an unsurveyed karst hex rolls 1d6: on a 1, the ground collapses — the unit falls 1 level and is immobilized until it spends 2 turns climbing out. The collapse is loud enough to be heard across the whole map.

complications.name: Acoustic Mirage
complications.text: Cave acoustics bend seismic and sound bearings by 15 to 40 degrees. The sensor net hears everything but pinpoints nothing. Two raid seasons ago, the perimeter reinforced the wrong rim for 20 minutes while the real attack came up the quarry road.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All seismic and acoustic contact bearings on the karst are skewed. The gamemaster rolls 1d6 per contact; on 1-3 the reported bearing is wrong by 30 degrees, in a direction the attacker chooses.

complications.name: Dust Columns
complications.text: In the dry season, moving faster than 30 kph on any unpaved surface raises a dust column visible at 20 kilometers. The raiders' approach will show — and so will every move you make in response, in real time, to anyone on the rim with binoculars.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any vehicle or 'Mech, on either side, moving faster than walking speed on unpaved ground is automatically detected anywhere on the map. A unit that moved fast to reach an ambush position loses the ambush.

complications.name: Ninety-Minute Gap
complications.text: Air cover has a 90-minute gap each cycle while the fighters recover, and it drifts through the day. The wing will not give you the gap schedule — that has been wing security policy since the last leak. You can work it out by watching, which means the enemy can too.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll for the raid's H-hour: on 1-4 of 1d6 it falls inside the air gap, and no aerospace support is available for the first 12 turns; on 5-6, one fighter pair arrives on turn 6.

decisionPoints.name: The Quarry Schedule
decisionPoints.context: Week 2: analysis shows that quarry blasting masks seismic detection across the entire southern karst for 40 minutes per blast, 3 blasts a week, on a published schedule. The quarry is also the district's biggest employer — 600 jobs — and its manager has friends in the planetary assembly. When the raid comes, it will almost certainly come during a blast window.

options.title: Shut the Quarry for the Season
advantages: The seismic mask disappears completely — the karst's best approach window closes
One decision, with no ongoing coordination to manage
disadvantages: 600 idled workers and an assembly inquiry within a month
The shutdown itself tells any watcher that you have figured out what the blasts were hiding
options.consequence: You restore your detection coverage at the cost of political standing. There is an employer-standing penalty unless a raid actually happens during the term, and the raiders simply switch to approaching under the acoustic-mirage instead.

costs.resource: political standing: 600 idled jobs and an assembly inquiry within a month
costs.risk: The employer-standing penalty stands unless the raid comes during the term — and the shutdown tells the watcher exactly what you have figured out

options.title: Synchronize: Your Eyes Open When the Ground Shakes
advantages: Every blast window gets an overwatch element pre-positioned on the southern rim — the blast schedule becomes your schedule too
The quarry keeps working, and the assembly stays uninterested
disadvantages: Three windows a week, every week, steadily wears down a limited roster
Because of the dust-column rule, pre-positioning means moving to the rim at walking pace, an hour early, every time
options.consequence: A raid during a blast window is met by ready forces, but the roster pays a steadily mounting fatigue cost. After week 6, overwatch elements operate at -1 effectiveness.

costs.resource: steady fatigue cost: 3 overwatch windows a week, every week, dropping to -1 effectiveness after week 6

options.title: Leave It — Instrument the Quarry Road Instead
advantages: Wire-laid sensors and a vehicle barrier on the single road through the quarry cut cost nothing week to week
No political contact, no ongoing fatigue, and no schedule that can leak
disadvantages: Covers the road, but not the open karst that the blasts also mask
Accepts that a force crossing the open karst during a blast window arrives undetected if it avoids the road
options.consequence: The road approach is closed for good, but the open-karst approach during blast windows stays open, and the fight begins wherever the raiders come up out of the sinkholes.

costs.risk: A force crossing the open karst during a blast window arrives undetected if it avoids the road

entries.event: Alarm: a dog team and post nine report movement in the sinkholes, 800 meters south of the wire. The acoustic net gives three bearings that cannot all be right.
The ready section moves to the karst rim fighting positions, and the depot's fire-suppression crews move to the pump stations.
The rim intercept line must be occupied by now. After this point, raiders who have emerged have continuous low-ground cover all the way to the wire.
Raiders who were not intercepted reach Tank Row Alpha and start setting fire to the tanks. Each 5 minutes they hold it burns 8-10 percent of storage.
The air-gap question is answered: wing fighters are on station now if the gap was missed, or it is 70 more minutes if it was not.
The raid force begins withdrawing through the karst regardless of the result. Pursuing them into the sinkholes means fighting on their survey, not yours.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The rim intercept line must be manned by T+7:00. Raiders who reach Tank Row Alpha at T+12:00 burn 8 to 10 percent of storage for every 5 minutes they hold it, so the 10 percent damage ceiling on the primary objective is gone almost the moment the first fire is set.

opforSketch.composition: A {TARGET_FACTION} raiding force: one Veteran 'Mech lance (fast mediums, energy-weapon biased, with at least one unit able to start fires) plus 1-2 squads of pathfinder infantry already in the karst, equipped with the survey your side does not have. Possibly a second lance in overwatch if the threat roll runs high.
opforSketch.behavior: Fire-mission tactics: the target is the fuel tanks, not your force. The pathfinders mark the route and the breach point; the lance runs it at speed, sets Tank Row Alpha on fire, and withdraws into the sinkholes under the acoustic mirage. It engages your defenders only when they are in the way, and breaks off any pursuit at the karst rim, where its survey advantage begins.

forks.name: OPERATION PLUMB LINE
forks.trigger: Depot under 10 percent damage and pathfinder materials recovered.
forks.consequence: The karst survey in the raiders' kit was made with civilian ground radar — the same contractor model the quarry leases. Counterintelligence opens a quiet file and your command provides the muscle for the arrest it ends in: a SECURITY_DUTY coda among people you have been waving to for a month.

forks.name: OPERATION GROUNDED WING
forks.trigger: Storage losses exceed 40 percent or the pump house is destroyed.
forks.consequence: The wing flies quarter rations for a season and {TARGET_FACTION} knows it. The next raid arrives in company strength against a depot that cannot fuel its own air cover — GARRISON_DUTY under an empty sky.

forks.name: OPERATION THIN MIXTURE
forks.trigger: Depot held but storage losses between 10 and 40 percent.
forks.consequence: Fuel rationing pits the wing's sortie schedule against ground-force training allocations for 60 days; your command escorts the emergency tanker convoys up from the southern refinery — 300 kilometers of dry-season road, dust columns all the way.

storyElementSeed: Each morning the perimeter sergeant drops a pebble down the new sinkhole by post nine and counts; the duty log has a column for it now — depth by echo, in seconds — and the column has been getting longer all month.

merc.objectives.primary: The depot must be standing at the end of the term with damage under 10 percent of storage capacity — that is the payment trigger in Section 6, and the employer's assessors measure the tanks by volume, not by how hard you tried. Read the karst survey clause in Annex D twice: damage from ground collapse to your equipment is classified as environmental, not combat, and environmental damage is not reimbursed.

phases.name: POSTURE — LEARNING THE GROUND THAT LIES
phases.lead: The first weeks are spent learning what not to trust: which sensor bearings to ignore, which sinkholes are new, which blast windows matter. The depot has survived 9 raid seasons on exactly this kind of caution, and the sergeants who kept it standing are your teachers.

dataBlock.Perimeter rhythm: 14 posts walked in 4-hour stints; dog teams on the karst rim at dawn and dusk; ground radar re-survey 1 sector per week
dataBlock.Karst survey: Cave system mapped to 60 percent, survey age 6 years; {NEW_SINKHOLES} new collapses last wet season, connections unbudgeted
dataBlock.Quarry mask: 3 blasts per week on a published schedule; each blast blanks seismic detection across the southern karst for 40 minutes
dataBlock.Air cover: 90-minute recovery gap per cycle, drifting through the day, unpublished even to you

phases.protocol: Bearing discipline, standing order: do not act on any acoustic or seismic contact on the karst without a second source confirming it — a dog team, a visual sighting, or a radar return. Log single-source contacts with the time and an estimate of the bearing skew, then leave them alone. The rim reinforced the wrong side for 20 minutes once, and the depot cannot afford to make that mistake again.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Reconstructing the air gap from the rim: how a patient observer plots the fighter recovery cycle in 2 weeks of watching, and what that tells you about how long the raiders' pathfinders have had to make their survey.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — OUT OF THE DOLINES
phases.lead: The raid comes up out of ground you never finished mapping, behind a bearing the karst has already bent. The rim intercept line by T+7:00 is the whole defense — miss it, and the low ground carries the raiders to the wire while Tank Row Alpha burns a percentage at a time.

dataBlock.Intercept deadline: Rim fighting positions occupied by T+7:00; emerged raiders have continuous low-ground cover to the wire after
dataBlock.Burn rate: Tank Row Alpha from T+12:00: 8-10 percent of storage per 5 minutes of possession; the 10 percent ceiling dies at first ignition plus one
dataBlock.Air question: Resolves T+20:00 — fighters on station, or 70 more minutes of empty sky
dataBlock.Raider exit: Withdrawal through the karst at T+45:00 regardless of result

routes.name: LIME
routes.desc: Paved perimeter ring road to the southern rim positions, 5.2km.
routes.tradeoff: Full speed with no dust column, so your move stays unseen — but it is the long way around, 4 minutes slower to the rim than the direct track.

routes.name: SPALL
routes.desc: A direct graded track across the surveyed edge of the karst, 2.1km.
routes.tradeoff: The fastest line to the intercept positions, but above 30kph it raises a dust column visible at 20km, and any position it reaches loses its ambush value the moment you arrive.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Defending a fuel farm without shooting into it: fields of fire that keep tracer and missile backblast out of the tank rows, and why the rim line exists so the fight never has to happen at the wire.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — WHAT THE KARST KEEPS
phases.lead: Pursuing the raiders into the sinkholes means fighting on their survey, and the standing order forbids it. The phase after the fight is recovery and forensics: the pathfinders' route, marked and then abandoned, is the bonus objective sitting on the ground — for as long as the dry wind leaves it readable.

dataBlock.Pursuit ceiling: No unit goes past the karst rim; beyond it the raiders have a survey and you do not
dataBlock.Forensic window: Route markers, cave-entry sign, and track casts legible 48-72 hours before dust-fill
dataBlock.The survey question: Pathfinder records recovered intact identify the contractor-model ground radar that made them — counterintelligence's thread to pull

sidebarKernel.kernel: Damage assessment by tankage: what 8 percent of storage means against the wing's sortie schedule, and the pump-house dependencies that decide whether 8 percent is an inconvenience or a season.

skeleton: security detail must keep industrial power unbroken while the only commanding terrain is bureaucratically out of reach and the decisive moment arrives as one ambiguous conveyance that may be cargo or assault
inspiration: Norwegian heavy-water plant defence at Vemork's gorge shelf, 1943
title: OPERATION COLD LEDGER
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The asset is the metallurgical plant: a specialty alloy works sitting on a gorge shelf 400 meters above the river, and the only source of two crucible-grade alloys that {EMPLOYER}'s armor plants upstream cannot run without. The contract is plant security, 120 days, signed with the corporation rather than the Commonwealth — which matters, because corporations write their own contract annexes, and this one wrote a masterpiece: your authorized operating area ends at the centerline of the river. The far rim of the gorge — 900 meters away across open air, with clear observation and direct fire onto every square meter of the shelf — is county land, and putting armed mercenaries there requires a provincial permit the employer has not obtained and is in no hurry to get. The terrain problem is vertical. One switchback road climbs the gorge wall to the shelf: 8 hairpins, single lane, 26 minutes for a 'Mech walking it carefully, with Hairpin Four the only wide spot where two machines can pass. One freight funicular runs from the river terminal up to the shelf on a 14-minute cycle, rated for 30 tons. That is the entire list of ways up and down — anything on top cannot get down quickly, anything below cannot get up quickly, and that applies to you exactly as much as to the enemy. The gorge fights your sensors too: wind shear gusting to 90 kph makes VTOL flying a gamble and jump-jet work near the rim a gamble of its own, and the river's roar fills the whole sound spectrum so completely that the plant's own seismographs are mounted on rubber to filter it out. The plant cannot stop. Crucible pours run on a 9-day cycle, and a power cut longer than 20 minutes mid-cycle freezes the molten metal in the crucibles, turning the line into 2,000 tons of scrap that takes a year to replace. So a lockdown is never an option — the alloy does not wait. Here is the threat, from {NPC:intel-source}, and it is 11 days old and only moderately confirmed. A sabotage cell with {TARGET_FACTION} markings has moved through two border worlds in this province doing exactly this kind of work: charges on power infrastructure, timed with a deniable raiding force to cover their escape. Closer to home, freight-manifest anomalies at the river terminal have been flagged 3 times in 2 weeks, with car weights disagreeing with the paperwork by 180 to 420 kilograms. The plant's own security chief logged those anomalies, resents your contract, and has not shared the gate rosters. The waiting here runs on a timetable: the noon whistle, the funicular's 14-minute cycle, and the pour-cycle calendar pinned up in your operations room with day 9 circled in someone else's red ink.

objectives.primary: Get the crucible line through all its pour cycles during the contract term — no power interruption longer than 20 minutes, and no damage to the crucibles, transformers, or the funicular's drive house.
objectives.secondary: Keep the switchback road and the funicular under friendly control throughout any engagement.
objectives.bonus: Identify the inside source feeding the cell. The weight anomalies required terminal access that no outsider has.

complications.name: The Far Rim
complications.text: Across 900 meters of open gorge, the far rim looks down on everything: gate rotations, pour schedules, your people at breakfast. It is outside your authorized operating area, so anything placed there — observers, a recoilless team, a laser — is legally protected by the very contract you signed.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The attacker may place 1-2 observation or fire-support elements on the far rim at setup. Defending units may not cross the river centerline without triggering the COMPROMISED outcome gate, unless the permit decision point resolved otherwise.

complications.name: Wind Shear
complications.text: Gorge winds gust to 90 kph with no pattern. The plant's VTOL pad is rated for calm mornings only, and jumping near the rim is a gamble where the penalty for losing is a 400-meter fall.
complications.mechanicalEffect: No VTOL operations during the engagement. Any jump that begins or ends within 3 hexes of the rim requires a control roll at +2; on a failure, the unit scatters 1d3 hexes toward the gorge.

complications.name: The Pour Does Not Stop
complications.text: On day 9 of each cycle, the crucibles pour and the plant draws its maximum power load. The line cannot be paused, the workers cannot be cleared out, and a 20-minute power cut turns the plant to scrap. Every defensive plan has to work around 600 civilians doing shift work inside the objective.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During a pour-day engagement, all defending fire inside the plant footprint puts the line at risk: any stray-shot result that hits plant infrastructure counts double against the primary objective's damage threshold.

complications.name: The House Chief
complications.text: The plant's security chief treats your contract as an insult and your requests as optional. Gate rosters, badge records, and the terminal's manifest archive arrive late, redacted, or not at all — right up until the day everything is on fire, when they all arrive at once and too late to help.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The bonus objective cannot be completed before the engagement unless the defender wins a cooperation roll (one attempt per week, 5+ on 1d6, +1 after any proven anomaly). The inside source acts at H-hour regardless.

decisionPoints.name: The Permit Question
decisionPoints.context: Week 2: your survey confirms the far rim is the only place from which the plant can be watched or hit with direct fire without climbing the switchback. The provincial permit takes 30 days through official channels, and the filing announces your interest in the rim to anyone reading the county records. The employer's lawyer advises patience. That lawyer works in a building with no gorge under it.

options.title: File for the Permit
advantages: Legal cover for operating on the rim from day 30 onward
The public filing itself may scare off a cell that reads public records
disadvantages: 30 days of exposure before the permit comes through
The filing signals that you have identified the rim, so a careful enemy speeds up or relocates
options.consequence: From day 30, the defender can operate freely on the rim, but the attacker's timetable moves up and the attack probably arrives before the permit does.

costs.risk: The public filing signals the rim, so a careful enemy speeds up or relocates during your 30-day wait

options.title: Quiet Overwatch — No Permit
advantages: Eyes on the rim now — in civilian clothes, with binoculars and a radio, deniable up to a point
No public filing, nothing that signals your interest
disadvantages: An armed response from the rim is still unauthorized; your observers can watch a fire mission set up and report it, but not stop it
If county police find your people, the contract's compliance clause kicks in — and the house chief would be glad to make that call
options.consequence: The defender gets warning of any emplacement on the rim, but to actually engage it you need either the switchback's mortar pit (indirect and slow) or to cross your operating area, which triggers the COMPROMISED gate.

costs.resource: a 2-person watch in civilian clothes on county land, around the clock, deniable up to a point
costs.risk: If the county discovers them, the compliance clause activates — and the house chief makes the call himself

options.title: Cede the Rim, Harden the Shelf
advantages: Every C-bill and work-hour goes into netting, berms, and moving the transformer yard out of the rim's line of sight
No legal exposure at all; the contract is performed exactly as written
disadvantages: You cannot harden away observation — your schedules and rotations stay visible
A fire-support element on the rim at H-hour fires for the first 3 turns without any reply
options.consequence: The plant's physical vulnerability to rim fire drops sharply, but the information leak continues, and the fight opens with the enemy knowing your positions to the minute.

costs.risk: You cannot harden away observation; H-hour opens with rim fire going unanswered for 3 turns

decisionPoints.name: The Car on the Cable
decisionPoints.context: H-hour: charges are found on the transformer conduits, there is small-arms fire at the river terminal below, and the funicular is halfway up, carrying either the day's flux shipment or the breaching team, 7 minutes from docking at the shelf. Its weight readout disagrees with the manifest by 390 kilograms. The drive house is yours: you can stop the car, bring it in, or cut its power for good.

options.title: Halt It Mid-Span
advantages: Whatever is in the car is left hanging 200 meters over the river, out of the fight indefinitely
You defer the decision — the car can be brought up later, under control, once the shooting stops
disadvantages: If the car holds flux and terminal workers, they are left hanging in 90 kph gusts while the battle plays out
A skilled team can rappel down lines; stopping the car mid-span is an inconvenience to them, not a locked door
options.consequence: The car's contents are out of play for at least 1d6+4 turns. If the breaching team is aboard, it ropes down to the lower wall and enters the fight late, from an unexpected height.

costs.risk: If they are workers, they hang in 90 kph gusts while the battle plays out — and rappel lines make stopping the car an inconvenience, not a locked door

options.title: Dock It Under Guns
advantages: The question answers itself in 7 minutes, at a terminal where you have already set your fields of fire
If they are workers, they step off safely and say so
disadvantages: A breaching team docking into your gunline means a breaching charge going off at your gunline
Two units committed to receiving the car are two units not at the transformer fight
options.consequence: The contents are resolved right away, either violently or harmlessly; either way, the transformer defense is short-handed for the first 4 turns.

costs.resource: two units committed to receiving the car; the transformer fight runs short-handed for 4 turns
costs.risk: A breaching team docking into your gunline is a breaching charge at your gunline

options.title: Cut Drive Power
advantages: The funicular stops being useful to anyone for the rest of the engagement
The simplest possible order at the worst possible moment
disadvantages: You cut the plant's freight lifeline with the flux shipment the pour needs somewhere on the cable
If the pour misses its flux feed by more than 3 hours, the cycle aborts — a self-inflicted hit to the primary objective
options.consequence: The cable threat is gone, but a 3-hour resupply clock starts against the pour cycle, and the switchback becomes the only route for everything, both sides, for the rest of the mission.

costs.resource: the freight lifeline is cut: the funicular is out of play for the rest of the mission
costs.risk: If the pour misses its flux feed by 3 hours the cycle aborts — a self-inflicted hit to the primary objective

entries.event: Alarm: shaped charges are found on the transformer conduits during a routine conduit walk, and at the same moment small-arms fire is reported at the river terminal.
The shelf reaction element moves to the transformer yard, and the switchback gate is sealed at Hairpin One.
The funicular car, halfway up at the alarm, docks at the shelf if it was not stopped.
A hostile 'Mech element climbing the switchback reaches Hairpin Four — the last point where a blocking position can hold the road with fewer machines than the attacker has.
If unblocked, the climb is complete: hostile machines are on the shelf among 600 shift workers and live crucibles.
If plant power was cut at H-hour, restoration must be complete by now — the melt's 20-minute thermal margin, plus a little grace, runs out.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Hairpin Four must be blocked by T+16:00 and plant power restored by T+35:00. Miss the first and the fight moves into the crucible hall; miss the second and there is nothing left worth fighting for.

opforSketch.composition: A deniable mixed force using {TARGET_FACTION}-pattern equipment with the serial numbers ground off: 1 sabotage cell of 6-10 specialists (Veteran) already inside the fence under contractor cover, 1 light raid lance (20-40 tons, Regular) staged in the river valley to climb the switchback or cover the extraction, and an optional fire-support team on the far rim if the complication is in play.
opforSketch.behavior: Sabotage first: the charges are the mission, the lance is the backup, the rim is the overwatch. If the charges go off on schedule, the lance never engages at all. If they are interrupted, the lance climbs to extract the cell, and only accepts a Hairpin Four fight if the cell is still alive to extract. Nobody in this force dies for ground.

forks.name: OPERATION SILENT PARTNER
forks.trigger: All pour cycles completed, plant intact, and the inside source identified or captured.
forks.consequence: The source's payments trace to a holding company two jumps away that also brokers the employer's competitor contracts. The corporation quietly extends your term and asks for discreet escort of its counsel's evidentiary mission — SECURITY_DUTY where the enemy wears suits.

forks.name: OPERATION MARGIN CALL
forks.trigger: Crucible line frozen, or plant damage exceeding the primary threshold.
forks.consequence: The corporation invokes liquidated damages and the dispute goes to the Mercenary Review Board; pending judgment, the unit's bond rating drops one band and the only contracts on offer are the kind written for units that cannot say no.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET SETTLEMENT
forks.trigger: Defending forces operated armed on the far rim without permit, and it surfaced.
forks.consequence: County charges, provincial review, and an employer suddenly unable to recall who suggested vigilance. The settlement terms include 60 days of unpaid 'community security assistance' in the county seat — RIOT_DUTY-adjacent work, performed politely, while the lawyers eat the margin.

storyElementSeed: The noon whistle sounds and the funicular starts down on schedule; at the upper terminal a guard checks the manifest against the car's weight readout, and for the third time this week the two numbers do not quite agree.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: The metallurgical plant's crucible line must complete the quarter's pour schedule without interruption — the alloy is already sold in advance, and any shortfall hits the Commonwealth's armor program at a political cost, not just a commercial one. The operating-area annex was negotiated by the corporation's own lawyers against their own security interest; this is noted for the record, which is where it will stay.

H_HOUR_DAY.unit: day of the pour cycle when the attack comes

resourceGates.appliesTo: Cede the Rim, Harden the Shelf
resourceGates.lackingText: With the treasury under 15,000, hardening shrinks to just transformer-yard netting at 4,000 C-bills — the gates, the rotations, and the people at breakfast all stay in the rim's line of sight.

phases.name: THE LEDGER — TIMETABLE WATCH
phases.lead: Everything on the shelf runs on a published schedule — pours, whistles, the funicular's 14-minute cycle — and the defense is about learning which departures from it matter. Three weight anomalies in 2 weeks say the enemy is already using the timetable; the question is which part of it.

dataBlock.Pour cycle: 9 days; day 9 is maximum load; a 20-minute power cut mid-cycle converts the line to 2,000 tons of scrap
dataBlock.Mobility ledger: Switchback: 8 hairpins, single lane, 26 minutes walking, Hairpin Four the only passing point. Funicular: 14-minute cycle, 30-ton rating
dataBlock.Anomaly record: Car weight versus manifest: 3 discrepancies in 2 weeks, 180-420kg each, all logged by plant security, none explained
dataBlock.The rim: 900m across open air, clean observation and direct fire onto the shelf, outside the authorized operating area

phases.protocol: Weight protocol, in place from week 1: every funicular car is weighed at both terminals against its manifest, and any difference over 150kg holds the car at the lower terminal for a hand inspection before it rides up. Gate rosters and manifest archives are requested from plant security in writing every week, and every refusal is logged — building a documented record in advance, in case it is needed.

sidebarKernel.kernel: What 390 kilograms could be: 2 crates of flux that do not exist, or 1 breaching kit and the team to use it — the manifest math that turns a freight clerk's column of numbers into a threat assessment.

phases.name: H-HOUR — THE VERTICAL FIGHT
phases.lead: Charges on the conduits, fire at the terminal below, and the car halfway up carrying 390 kilograms of unanswered question: the fight is waged up and down 400 meters of gorge wall, on two routes that each take one machine at a time. Hairpin Four by T+16:00, power restored by T+35:00 — miss either and the plant decides the battle for you.

dataBlock.Blocking deadline: Hairpin Four held by T+16:00 — the last point where fewer machines hold the road against more
dataBlock.Power deadline: Restoration complete by T+35:00; the melt's thermal margin plus grace ends there
dataBlock.The car: Mid-span at alarm, 7 minutes from shelf docking, 390kg over manifest
dataBlock.Pour-day constraint: 600 shift workers inside the objective; stray-shot damage to plant infrastructure counts double against the primary threshold

routes.name: SWITCHBACK
routes.desc: The road: 8 hairpins up the gorge wall, single lane, 26 minutes for a careful 'Mech.
routes.tradeoff: The only path for armor and the only way out for anything heavy. Whoever holds Hairpin Four controls the whole route — and a wreck at any hairpin closes the road to both sides for hours.

routes.name: CABLE
routes.desc: The funicular: river terminal to shelf in 14 minutes, 30-ton car, drive house at the top in friendly hands.
routes.tradeoff: Faster than the road, but rated for only one light vehicle or one squad at a time. Whoever rides it arrives at the mercy of whoever holds the drive house, and cutting its power mid-fight starts the 3-hour flux clock against your own pour.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Fighting in a vertical box: why the gorge turns every reinforcement decision into a 26-minute commitment, and what the rim's sightlines do to any plan that forgets to look up.

phases.name: SETTLEMENT — THE POUR AND THE PROOF
phases.lead: The contract is satisfied by a completed pour schedule, not by a body count, and the quarter ends with the line running and the inside source named — or with lawyers. The weight anomalies, the gate rosters, and whatever the fight left on the cable are all evidence now, and evidence has to have an unbroken chain of custody.

dataBlock.Pour completion: All cycles in the 120-day term; any interrupted cycle is a 1-year replacement horizon talking
dataBlock.Source investigation: The anomalies required terminal access from inside; the suspect pool is the terminal's own roster plus whoever amended its paperwork
dataBlock.Cooperation state: The house chief's archives arrive all at once after the fire — cross-reference against your own weekly request log to find what was withheld, and when

sidebarKernel.kernel: The melt as a hostage: thermal margins, crucible preheat economics, and why the works engineer's 20-minute figure is the one number in this contract nobody gets to negotiate.

assetDetails.detail: Mid-cycle, the melt holds 2,000 tons at temperature on grid power, with a 20-minute thermal margin. The plant's own backup power covers 4 minutes of that, and nothing covers the rest. The line cannot pause, cannot be cleared of its 600 workers, and cannot be defended by anything that puts the transformers it runs on at risk.

Twenty-two years at the plant. He logged the weight anomalies himself, before your contract existed, and resents that the corporation answered them by bringing in outsiders. The way to move him is his pride, not his cooperation: requests framed as backing up his own findings clear in hours; requests framed as checking up on his failures arrive redacted or never.

There is one operator per shift in the drive house, and the night man is rumored to have gambling debts in the river town. It is unverified — but the weight anomalies all rode night cars, and 180 to 420 kilograms got past somebody. Check him out before H-hour answers the question for you, on its own schedule.

skeleton: garrison must keep a food reserve sealed against a desperate crowd under a hard casualty cap while two rival authorities issue contradictory written orders that will both be remembered
inspiration: Tsarist garrison facing the Petrograd bread riots, February 1917
title: OPERATION ASH CURFEW
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The order assigning your command to civil security in the ring district of the planetary capital is one page long. The situation it drops you into is older than the order, older than the garrison, and it is fundamentally about water. Six weeks ago the ring district's main pumping station failed — a 70-year-old turbine the district has requested replacement parts for 4 times in 9 years, denied every time in favor of military priorities. Water rationing followed; then the grain ration was cut {RATION_CUT_PERCENT} percent to cover a levy for the front; then the first market riot, 11 days ago, which the local militia broke up badly. Three civilians died. The district has not been quiet since, and the ISF district office reads that unrest as enemy work: leaflets in three different print styles, slogans painted on walls in paint nobody sells locally, and 2 confirmed agitator cells working inside a hungry, angry population that hides them well. That cell count comes from {NPC:intel-source} and is 4 days old. Treat the count of two as fairly solid, but who is backing the cells is still a guess. Your terrain problem stands on 9-meter concrete legs: the ring viaduct, an elevated freight monorail loop circling the district, with the markets underneath it where 40,000 people trade, line up, and gather. The viaduct piers were not built to withstand combat. A 'Mech-scale weapon hit on a pier risks bringing a span down in a chain reaction onto whatever crowd is beneath it — and there is always a crowd beneath it. Under the viaduct, you do not fire heavy weapons; that is a structural fact, not a tactical preference. You have to learn the district's daily rhythm: water lines form at 0500 at the 6 working standpipes, the markets fill by 0800, the curfew bell rings from the viaduct pylons at dusk, and the ISF's informers report which stalls were slow to pack up. Crowds here form in 20 minutes off a single rumor, and the rumor travels faster than your vehicles — the last riot started with a false report of a child drowned by a militia water cannon, and the truth, arriving 2 hours later, found that nobody was listening anymore. The granary on the ring plaza holds the district's 60-day food reserve. The militia armory stands 800 meters from it. The ISF wants the curfew enforced hard; the civil governor wants the pumping station fixed and the soldiers kept out of sight; the Coordinator presumably wants both, and you hold the only force in the district capable of either. Your engineers could have the turbine running in 9 days. Your 'Mechs could hold the plaza in 9 minutes. Choose carefully which one you do first; the district is watching.

objectives.primary: Keep the ring plaza granary secure — no breach, no loss of the 60-day reserve — and keep civilian deaths caused by security forces to no more than 10 for the whole deployment.
objectives.secondary: Keep the militia armory's weapons out of the crowd's hands, and identify or neutralize both agitator cells.
objectives.bonus: Get the ring district's pumping station back in service during the deployment, which addresses the grievance at its root.

complications.name: The Viaduct
complications.text: Every viaduct pier holds up a live span over occupied market ground. Pier damage spreads in a chain reaction: one span falling is 300 tons coming down into the market below. You cannot safely fire any weapon heavier than small arms within 2 hexes of a pier, and everyone inclined to riot knows where the piers are.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Heavy-weapon fire within 2 hexes of a pier risks a collapse (1d6: collapse on 1-2), and any collapse causes mass civilian casualties — the primary objective fails immediately. Crowds and cells deliberately stay inside this zone.

complications.name: Rumor Velocity
complications.text: A rumor crosses the district in 20 minutes; an official correction takes 2 hours and arrives too late to matter. Any security action — justified or not — produces a hostile, distorted version of itself within the hour.
complications.mechanicalEffect: After each engagement or crowd action, roll 1d6: on 1-3 a false atrocity rumor spreads, raising the Escalation Index by 1 regardless of how your forces actually behaved. The Index starts at 2; at 8, a general uprising begins and the FAILURE gate is near.

complications.name: Militia in the Middle
complications.text: The local militia lives in the district it polices. Eleven days ago it fired on its own neighbors, and it has not finished working out how it feels about that. Militia units may obey, hesitate, or stand aside — and the crowd tests them first, every time.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each militia unit makes a check at first crowd contact in an engagement (1d6): on 1-2 it stands aside, on 3-4 it holds position but will not advance, on 5-6 it does as ordered. ISF observers log every result.

complications.name: Honest Water, Hidden Fish
complications.text: The agitator cells operate inside a population with real grievances. Mass arrests catch the genuinely thirsty and desperate while the agitators slip away; catching the right people needs intelligence the ISF does not have and the crowd will not give while the standpipes stay dry.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Cell-hunting actions only succeed after the Escalation Index has been dropped below its starting value, or the pumping-station repair has begun. Before that, sweeps raise the Index by 1 and turn up only decoys.

decisionPoints.name: The Plaza Crowd
decisionPoints.context: Day {FLASHPOINT_DAY}, 0930: a water line becomes a crowd, the crowd grows to 5,000, and its leading edge reaches the granary fence within the hour. The grain is inside; thirst and 11 days of grief are outside; the agitators are somewhere in the middle, working the crowd. The ISF liaison wants armor on the plaza now. The civil governor is on the line telling you the opposite.

options.title: Weight on Display — 'Mechs to the Plaza
advantages: No crowd in {EMPLOYER} charges a line of BattleMechs; the fence holds without a shot fired
The ISF rates the response as decisive, and the granary question is settled at once
disadvantages: The image of 'Mechs facing thirsty civilians is the best leaflet the agitators could ask for, and you printed it for them
Any mishap — a fall, a panic crush at the back of the crowd — becomes a massacre by rumor within the hour
options.consequence: The plaza clears today, but the Escalation Index rises by 2, and from now on every crowd action gathers under the viaduct piers, where your heavy units cannot follow.

costs.resource: Escalation Index +2, paid today and collected later under the piers
costs.risk: One mishap or a panic crush at the back of the crowd becomes a massacre by rumor within the hour

options.title: Militia Forward, 'Mechs Out of Sight
advantages: A human-scale response to a human-scale grievance gives the rumor less to feed on
If the militia performs well here, it starts to rebuild its own standing — and yours
disadvantages: The militia check rule applies at the worst possible moment
If the line breaks, the granary fence is just wire and momentum, and the 60-day reserve is 40 minutes from being gone
options.consequence: The militia's dice decide the day: success lowers the Escalation Index by 1; failure puts the crowd inside the fence with your reaction force 9 minutes away.

costs.resource: you stake the militia's credibility at the fence: the first-contact check decides whether the line holds
costs.risk: A broken line puts the crowd inside the wire with your reaction force 9 minutes away

options.title: Open the Standpipe Valves — Negotiate at the Fence
advantages: Releasing emergency water from the granary's own cistern answers the real grievance at the moment it matters
An officer at the fence with his helmet off is the one image the agitators cannot use against you
disadvantages: Releasing the cistern shortens how long the granary can hold out under siege by 9 days
If the crowd reads the gesture as weakness, they test the fence while your posture is soft
options.consequence: If the crowd disperses on the water, the Escalation Index drops by 2; but the agitator cells, denied their moment, move up their armory attack — the T+60:00 event becomes T+40:00.

costs.resource: the granary cistern's siege endurance: -9 days
costs.risk: If the gesture is read as weakness, the crowd tests the fence while your posture is soft

decisionPoints.name: The Curfew Order
decisionPoints.context: The ISF district office sends a written request: full curfew enforcement, markets closed at the bell, violators detained, the area under the viaduct swept every night. The civil governor's office sends a written objection the same afternoon. Both documents are addressed to you, and whichever office you turn down will remember it.

options.title: Enforce in Full
advantages: The ISF opens up its cell intelligence — their files significantly improve your odds on the secondary objective
Night-time gatherings become impossible, so the cells lose the hours they use to organize
disadvantages: The markets are how the district distributes food; closing them sharply at the bell makes the very hunger that fills the plaza worse
Nightly sweeps under the piers, in the dark, among the stalls — each one is a rumor waiting for a spark
options.consequence: The secondary objective gains ISF intelligence support, but the Escalation Index rises by 1 for each week of full enforcement.

costs.resource: Escalation Index: +1 per week of full enforcement
costs.risk: Every nightly sweep under the piers is a rumor waiting for a spark

options.title: Enforce Selectively — Markets Exempt Until the Late Bell
advantages: Food keeps moving; the curfew restricts gatherings without cutting off dinner
Both offices can claim partial satisfaction, which is ultimately what offices want
disadvantages: The ISF records the exemption as weakness and shares its files at half speed
The cells learn the geography of the exemption faster than the ISF learns the cells
options.consequence: The Escalation Index is unchanged, but the agitator cells gain the market hours as cover, and the armory attack keeps its original timing while adding 1 more participating cell.

costs.resource: ISF files arrive at half speed
costs.risk: The cells learn the geography of the exemption faster than the ISF learns the cells

options.title: Decline Enforcement — Soldiers Guard, Police Police
advantages: Your force guards the granary, armory, and pumping station without becoming the public face of the curfew
The civil governor's gratitude takes practical forms: labor, priority on the turbine parts, quiet streets near your cantonment
disadvantages: The ISF files a formal note on your command's reliability — the kind that resurfaces in future postings
Without curfew pressure, the cells organize openly after dark
options.consequence: The bonus objective's timeline improves by 3 days (the governor's parts priority), but the ISF note applies a standing -1 to your employer assessment unless both cells are delivered before the deployment ends.

costs.resource: an ISF reliability note: a standing -1 on your employer assessment unless both cells are delivered
costs.risk: Without curfew pressure, the cells organize openly after dark

entries.event: Alarm: the granary fence is under crowd pressure at the ring plaza, an estimated 5,000 and growing, with simultaneous reports of stall fires under the viaduct pulling the militia's night section away.
The reaction force must be moving by now — once the crowd passes 6,000, the plaza approach roads jam with handcarts and people fleeing.
Fence assessments give it 20 more minutes under sustained pressure. Agitator marshals are visible, directing the crowd toward the gate side.
The armory probe begins (earlier if the cistern was released): 20-40 armed cell members test the armory's side gate while its garrison is watching the plaza.
If unreinforced, the granary gate fails under the pressure, and the reserve starts being lost at 2 percent for every minute the gate is open.
The main armory attempt (original timing): a breach team with cutting equipment at the weapons vault. Past this point, the riot is armed.
