reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The granary gate must be reinforced by T+45:00 and the armory secured by T+60:00. Miss the first and the district starves in 60 days; miss the second and it is armed tonight.

opforSketch.composition: Less an army than a crowd in motion: crowd masses of 3,000-8,000 (treat them as moving terrain that also witnesses everything), 2 agitator cells of 15-25 operatives each (Green, fanatic, with small arms and improvised incendiaries), 2-3 stolen militia security vehicles, and — if the Escalation Index passed 5 before H-hour — 1-2 converted industrial exoskeletons or LoaderMechs with welded-on armor plate.
opforSketch.behavior: The cells fight for images and weapons, not ground: they provoke you into firing near the piers, push crowds against the fences, and strike the armory when distraction is at its peak. The crowd itself follows water, grief, and rumor — drain the grievance and the cells are exposed; feed it and they disappear into the crowd.

forks.name: OPERATION FOREIGN HAND
forks.trigger: Granary and armory held, fatalities under threshold, both cells taken.
forks.consequence: Interrogation traces the paint, the print styles, and the money to a courier route running through a licensed trading house — a SECURITY_DUTY follow-on at the spaceport, watching cargo manifests with the ISF reading over your shoulder.

forks.name: OPERATION WINTER MUZZLE
forks.trigger: Civilian fatalities exceed threshold, a pier falls, or the armory is breached.
forks.consequence: The district rises in earnest and the ISF assumes direction of the response. Your command spends the winter holding intersections in a city that has stopped speaking to it, executing orders it did not write — GARRISON_DUTY in the ruins of its own deployment, threat sustained.

forks.name: OPERATION GRAY MARKET
forks.trigger: Granary held but cistern spent, or curfew weeks passed with the Index above start.
forks.consequence: An organized black market in grain and water emerges, run by people more competent than the agitators ever were. Escorting legitimate ration convoys through territory the gray market now taxes is the next deployment's texture — RIOT_DUTY's long tail.

storyElementSeed: At dusk the curfew bell rings from the viaduct pylons and the market packs itself away without hurry; one stall stays lit a quarter-hour longer by old arrangement — the tea seller, so the patrol has somewhere warm to end its round — and tonight the stall is dark.

merc.objectives.primary: The contract's casualty clause is explicit: the granary intact, civilian deaths caused by security forces capped at 10, and every death over the cap costs a 4 percent payment deduction plus a Mercenary Review Board notification. The employer has built restraint into the price. Hold the fence and hold your fire discipline; the second is what makes the first pay.

resourceGates.lackingText: With the treasury under 20,000, full enforcement goes ahead without militia stipends or supplies for detentions — the nightly sweeps run on your own roster alone, so you pay the full Escalation cost without the extra manpower.

phases.name: POSTURE — LEARNING THE QUEUES
phases.lead: The district's daily rhythm is your intelligence picture: standpipe lines at 0500, markets by 0800, the bell at dusk. The deployment's first days are spent learning what the ring district is watching for in your actions — and getting engineers to the pumping station, visibly, before anything else is done in your name.

dataBlock.Water arithmetic: 6 functioning standpipes for the district; queues form at 0500; the failed turbine is a 9-day repair for your engineers, parts permitting
dataBlock.Rumor mechanics: A rumor crosses the district in 20 minutes; official correction takes 2 hours and arrives dead
dataBlock.Escalation Index: Starts at 2; the general rising begins at 8; every action feeds it or starves it
dataBlock.The piers: No weapon above small-arms class within 2 hexes of a viaduct pier — the calculation is architectural, and the crowd knows the envelope better than your gunners

phases.protocol: Standing orders, district-wide: heavy weapons stay outside the pier zone without exception, and every security action of any size is followed within 30 minutes by a plain-language account over the standpipe loudspeakers — not to beat the rumor, which is impossible, but to put the true version on the record alongside it. Engineer work parties at the pumping station travel unarmed, with militia escort, in daylight, on a published schedule: letting people see the repair happen is itself the point.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The turbine as politics: what a 70-year-old machine needs, which 3 parts decide the 9-day estimate, and why the work being seen matters as much as the work being done.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — THE PLAZA
phases.lead: A water line becomes a crowd, the crowd grows to 5,000, and the granary fence becomes the place where the whole deployment is judged. The armory probe rides the distraction: the cells fight for images at the fence and for weapons at the side gate, and your response has to answer both without handing them either.

dataBlock.Crowd dynamics: 5,000 at the fence inside the hour, building toward {CROWD_PEAK}; approach roads jam past 6,000
dataBlock.Fence clock: Integrity gives 20 minutes under sustained press from T+25:00; gate fails at T+45:00 unreinforced; reserve loss 2 percent per minute of open gate
dataBlock.Armory clock: Probe at the side gate T+40:00-T+60:00 depending on the cistern decision; past T+60:00 the riot is armed
dataBlock.Distance ledger: Granary to armory 800m; reaction force 9 minutes from cantonment once the roads jam

routes.name: BELL
routes.desc: Under the viaduct spans, straight through the market to the ring plaza, 1.9km.
routes.tradeoff: Fastest by 11 minutes — but every meter of it is inside the pier zone, through the crowd's own ground, with 300-ton spans overhead.

routes.name: RIM
routes.desc: Outside the viaduct loop on the freight road, 3.4km, arriving from the armory side.
routes.tradeoff: Clear of the piers and the crowds, and it covers the armory on the way — but 11 minutes slower to the granary fence, and 11 minutes is half the time the fence has left.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Crush injuries at a fence line: what a panic compression at the crowd's rear does to the people at its front, and why the aid post is positioned before the 'Mechs are.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — DRAINING THE GRIEVANCE
phases.lead: The plaza empties one way or another, and what remains are the underlying problems that filled it: the turbine, the ration, and the two cells still working the crowd. The deployment is not resolved when the crowd disperses but when the water runs again — or when the ISF imposes its own version of resolution instead.

dataBlock.Turbine timeline: 9 days of engineer work from parts-in-hand; governor's parts priority shortens it 3 days; cell-hunting becomes possible only after repair begins or the Index drops below 2
dataBlock.Cell accounting: 2 cells, 15-25 operatives each; sweeps before the water runs yield decoys and +1 Index
dataBlock.The ledger: Fatalities against the cap of 10; the granary's 60-day reserve against the cistern's -9 days if it was spent

sidebarKernel.kernel: Fishing after the flood: how falling water exposes the cells — who keeps agitating when the grievance drains, and why the last leaflet's print style is the first real lead.

skeleton: security force must keep both infrastructure and strikers alive through an industrial standoff while an inflammatory escort order arrives on dubious authority and a single death tips standoff into catastrophe
inspiration: British Army deployment to the Clydeside shipyard strikes, 'Red Clydeside' 1919
title: OPERATION STILL FIRTH
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The isle yards build drive components the Commonwealth's shipping cannot do without, and for {STRIKE_DAY} days they have built nothing at all. The general strike is disciplined, photogenic, and draped in the separatist colors that make the Commonwealth's political officers reach for their files: 9,000 yard workers out, pickets at all three firth bridges — the North, the Middle, and the South — that connect the isle to the mainland city, and a strike committee that publishes its non-violence pledge every week in two languages. The committee means it. That is {NPC:intel-source}'s assessment, delivered with high confidence and current to within 48 hours: the committee polices its own pickets, confiscates alcohol, and hands provocateurs over to the constabulary with receipts. The threat is not the strike. The threat is the splinter group — a cell of 8 to 15 radicals, expelled from the movement 5 weeks ago, who have decided the cause needs a martyr and that the Commonwealth should be forced to provide one. What you know about this cell is 8 days old and only moderately confirmed. Mining explosives went missing from a quarry shipment 19 days ago: 240 kilograms, never recovered. Your command holds civil security for the bridge district under a provincial writ that three noble houses publicly opposed; the tri-vid crews outnumber your patrols at every bridgehead, and footage travels faster than your reports. The terrain problem is the bridges themselves: three spans, 60 years old, rated for freight traffic but not for deliberate demolition, and not for the weight of a panicked crowd packed shoulder to shoulder over cold water. The firth fog rolls in most nights at 2200 and hides the far bank; the picket camps glow through it, and anything that happens before 0700 happens unwitnessed except by whoever planned it. You will learn the waiting here: shift whistles that call no one to work, negotiation sessions that adjourn on schedule, pickets who share their fire with your sentries and talk about football, because the strike is just what mornings are now. The provincial governor's office has set a deadline — the yards reopen within {DEADLINE_DAYS} days, by settlement or by writ — and a ferry of replacement workers is being assembled on the mainland about as subtly as a brass band. Every party on the isle can read the calendar. The cell is reading it too: their chance for a usable martyr closes the moment the settlement is signed. Expect them before that happens.

objectives.primary: No bridge falls and no massacre happens: keep all three Firth spans intact, and keep civilian deaths caused by security operations at zero through the deployment.
objectives.secondary: The strike ends — by settlement or by lawful reopening — without the yards suffering sabotage that takes more than 30 days to repair.
objectives.bonus: Account for the splinter cell and all 240 kilograms of quarry explosive, with evidence good enough for an open court rather than a sealed file.

complications.name: Everything Is Filmed
complications.text: Tri-vid crews hold permanent positions at all three bridgeheads with relay vans live to the mainland city and, by tomorrow, to half the region's worlds. Every order you give is given on camera; every stumble becomes the evening's lead. The cell counts on this more than on the explosive.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All conduct and collateral penalties are doubled; any security action against unarmed persons triggers an immediate Escalation check regardless of justification. Defender actions taken in fog hours (2200-0700) avoid the cameras but also lack exculpatory footage if disputed later.

complications.name: The Committee's Discipline
complications.text: The strike committee is the best crowd control on the isle — 5 weeks of perfect picket order proves it. Treated as a partner, it can clear a bridgehead in 15 minutes. Treated as a suspect, it stops policing the pickets, and then the only discipline left at the barricades is yours.
complications.mechanicalEffect: While committee cooperation holds, crowd masses obey marshal direction and clear danger zones on request (15-minute clock). Any mass arrest, picket raid, or 'Mech deployment to a bridgehead breaks cooperation permanently.

complications.name: Missing Consignment
complications.text: 240 kilograms of mining explosive is enough to drop one span twice over or all three approaches once. The quarry's paperwork was altered by someone who understood it; the constabulary's suspect list has 11 names and the cell has at least one quartermaster on it nobody has listed.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The attacker has demolition resources sufficient for 2 major charge sets; discovery of either before emplacement requires the bonus-objective investigative track, not patrol luck.

complications.name: The Fog
complications.text: Most nights at 2200 the fog closes the firth to 80-meter visibility until 0700. Boats move unseen beneath the spans; the cameras film gray; your thermal optics read the water as a wall. The cell's quartermaster has a boat.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During fog hours: visual detection 80 meters, no camera evidence exists of any event, and waterborne movement beneath the bridges is detectable only by the bridge-mounted seismic sets if the defender emplaced them beforehand (one bridge per 48 hours of engineering work).

decisionPoints.name: The Ferry Question
decisionPoints.context: Day {DEADLINE_DAYS} minus two: the governor's office confirms the replacement-worker ferry sails at dawn for the South Bridge landing — through the picket line's heart, with cameras on both banks. The order to secure its landing arrives over a signature one rank too junior for an order this combustible. The strike committee has asked, formally and politely, whether you intend to escort it.

options.title: Secure the South Landing as Ordered
advantages: The writ is executed; the governor's office owns the outcome it demanded
Maximum force presence at the most predictable flashpoint — if the cell strikes there, you are already deployed
disadvantages: Soldiers clearing a peaceful picket for strikebreakers is the martyr-image the cell has waited 5 weeks for, no explosive required
Committee cooperation breaks the moment the first picket is moved
options.consequence: The landing succeeds under cameras; committee discipline ends district-wide, the Escalation environment hardens, and the cell gains 8,000 angry witnesses to disappear into.

costs.resource: committee cooperation: broken permanently — the only working crowd control on the isle stands down
costs.risk: The martyr-image is produced free of explosive, with your command in the frame

options.title: Divert the Ferry — Land at the Yard's Own Quay
advantages: The yard quay is inside the fence, picket-free, and reachable in fog with a harbor pilot
No picket confrontation, no footage, the writ technically satisfied
disadvantages: Splitting your force to hold the quay corridor in fog hours, exactly when the seismic sets say nothing about the water
The committee reads the maneuver within a day and the governor's office reads it as your initiative, not theirs
options.consequence: The confrontation is avoided and the cell's bridge window narrows — so the cell moves to its contingency: the quay corridor in fog, against your divided force.

costs.resource: force divided: the quay corridor held through fog hours the seismic sets do not cover
costs.risk: The cell's contingency meets your split force on the water at 80 meters' visibility

options.title: Request the Order in Writing, One Rank Up — and Buy a Night
advantages: A 24-hour pause for a signature is bureaucratically unimpeachable and tactically priceless
The committee, shown the courtesy, extends its own deadline discipline one more day — and one more day may be the settlement's margin
disadvantages: The governor's office logs the request as reluctance; provincial patrons of the writ begin asking about your contract's renewal language
If the cell strikes during the bought night, the pause becomes the inquiry's first exhibit
options.consequence: The ferry holds 24 hours; settlement probability improves materially, and the cell — reading the same calendar — moves its attack into the bought night, against bridges, quay, or neither.

costs.resource: provincial patrons of the writ begin asking about your contract's renewal language
costs.risk: If the cell strikes during the bought night, the pause becomes the inquiry's first exhibit

entries.event: Alarm — explosion on the Middle Bridge catwalk, 0240, fog at 80 meters; span standing but structural state unknown; picket camps at both ends waking into the noise.
Crowds from both picket camps converge on the Middle bridgeheads — 600 from the isle side, 400 from the mainland side, growing.
Cordons must be standing at both bridgeheads by now; past this point the crowd is on the damaged span in the dark and the question becomes load, not order.
Engineering assessment of the span completes — and the sweep for secondary charges, which doctrine says to expect, must be underway with the deck clear.
Earliest credible window for a second device elsewhere — the North and South approaches are unwatched to the degree your cordons stripped them.
Dawn and the cameras. Whatever the night produced is broadcast by 0800, framed by whoever moved fastest.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Both Middle Bridge bridgeheads must be cordoned by T+12:00. If they are not, a thousand people crowd onto a blast-weakened span in the fog, and the span can collapse under their weight. That is the worst thing that can happen in this whole deployment, so this deadline outranks every other clock here.

opforSketch.composition: The splinter cell: 8-15 operatives (Green-to-Regular, 2 with professional demolition training), 240kg of mining explosive in unknown division, 1 workboat, and — if the yards' gates fall open in any disorder — access to 2-3 shipyard industrial exoskeletons and a heavy crane 'Mech convertible to obstruction work. No will to stand and fight; every will to make you fire first.
opforSketch.behavior: Provocation doctrine: strike infrastructure at night, herd crowds toward your guns by day, and film everything. The cell aborts any action the committee's marshals witness — its war is with the Commonwealth, but its first enemy is the settlement, and its operations are timed to kill negotiations at their most hopeful.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET FIRTH
forks.trigger: All spans intact, zero attributable fatalities, cell and explosives accounted for.
forks.consequence: The settlement signs in the yard's union hall and your command is requested — by the committee, pointedly — as security for the signing. A SECURITY_DUTY coda under every camera on the isle, where the only weapon that matters is posture.

forks.name: OPERATION BITTER ISLE
forks.trigger: A span falls, or security operations produce fatalities on camera.
forks.consequence: {WORLD} gets its martyrs and the movement gets its proof. Sympathy strikes spread to 3 more worlds within the month. On the isle, the strike turns into an armed insurgency: sabotage, night ambushes, and no more peaceful pickets. Your next job here is fighting that insurgency, which is a far harder war than riot duty.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN HANDS
forks.trigger: Evidence recovered during the deployment indicates the cell was steered — funding or warning traced into a provincial office that wanted the strike broken ugly.
forks.consequence: Your command holds documentation that one patron needs destroyed and another needs published. Both will pay; both can hurt you; the Mercenary Review Board is two jumps away and the evidence locker is here. The next mission is conducted entirely in rooms.

storyElementSeed: On the picket line the night shift shares its brazier with the sentries across the barrier; nobody discusses the strike — they discuss the football, because the strike is what mornings are for, and the fog takes the far bank at ten exactly.

merc.objectives.primary: Zero attributable civilian fatalities and three standing bridges — those are the contract's twin absolutes, and the penalty schedule behind them was drafted by people who expect you to fail. The tri-vid coverage is not in the contract; treat it as a second employer who pays in reputation and forecloses without notice.

phases.name: POSTURE — THE PICKET CALENDAR
phases.lead: Five weeks of perfect picket discipline is the ground truth; the deployment's first work is keeping it that way. The committee is the best crowd control on the isle and the cameras are the second employer — both are managed by daylight, on the record, while the seismic sets go onto the bridges one fog-free 48 hours at a time.

dataBlock.The spans: North, Middle, South — 60 years old, freight-rated, not rated for engineered demolition or a packed panicked crowd
dataBlock.The missing: 240kg of mining explosive, gone 19 days; enough to drop one span twice or all three approaches once
dataBlock.Fog regime: 2200-0700 most nights, visibility 80m; no camera evidence exists of anything inside it
dataBlock.Engineering race: Bridge-mounted seismic sets: one bridge per 48 hours of work; the only detection that hears the water under the fog

phases.protocol: Committee liaison runs through the marshal of the day, met at 0900 at the Middle Bridge tea van — requests to clear a bridgehead go to the marshal, never to pickets directly, and the 15-minute clock has held 5 weeks because nobody has cheapened it. Fog-hours challenge for anyone on the spans: HARBOUR, answered LIGHT; the marshals carry the countersign too, because the worst event this deployment can produce is a sentry firing at a striker in the gray.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Telling the movement from the splinter: the committee polices its pickets with receipts — what the 8-to-15 expelled radicals lost when they were cast out, and the one resource they kept.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT — THE FOG NIGHT
phases.lead: An explosion on the Middle Bridge catwalk at 0240, fog at 80 meters, and a thousand people waking toward a blast-weakened span: the cordons at both bridgeheads by T+12:00 are the entire mission compressed into 12 minutes. Everything after — the sweep, the second device, the dawn broadcast — is decided by whether the crowd was kept off the deck.

dataBlock.Cordon deadline: Both Middle bridgeheads by T+12:00; past it the question becomes load, not order
dataBlock.Converging crowds: 600 from the isle camp, 400 from the mainland side, both growing
dataBlock.Secondary doctrine: Engineering assessment and second-charge sweep from T+30:00 with the deck clear; the North and South approaches stand unwatched in proportion to what the cordons stripped
dataBlock.The broadcast: Dawn at T+250:00 — whatever the night produced airs by 0800, framed by whoever moved fastest

routes.name: ESPLANADE
routes.desc: The riverfront road direct to the Middle bridgeheads, 1.1km from the security post.
routes.tradeoff: Fastest — and it runs through both picket camps, waking them into the path of your own cordon and adding the camps to the crowd you are racing.

routes.name: YARDGATE
routes.desc: Through the shipyard perimeter on the committee's gate keys, 2.3km, emerging beside the mainland bridgehead.
routes.tradeoff: Avoids the camps entirely and arrives from an unexpected side — but the keys are the committee's, asked for at 0245, and the asking is itself a test of 5 weeks of liaison.

sidebarKernel.kernel: A blast-weakened 60-year span: what the catwalk charge tells you about what the deck can still hold, and why the assessment cannot be rushed by anyone shouting about optics.

phases.name: RESOLUTION — THE SIGNING TABLE
phases.lead: The cell's window closes when the settlement signs, and every party on the isle is reading the same calendar. The endgame is run at two tables at once: the governor's deadline and ferry on one side, the evidence chain on the other — built for open court, because a closed file hands the movement its martyr by paperwork.

dataBlock.The deadline: Yards reopen within {DEADLINE_DAYS} days by settlement or writ; the replacement-worker ferry assembles on the mainland in plain sight
dataBlock.The cell's window: Closes at signature; expect the attack before it — their war is with the settlement first
dataBlock.Evidence standard: Recovered explosive and cell materials logged with constabulary countersignature at point of recovery, custody unbroken — fit for open court or not worth recovering

phases.protocol: Recovery protocol for the bonus objective: nothing touched without a constable present, every cache photographed in place, every kilogram weighed against the quarry's 240 and the running total published to the governor's office and the committee alike — the count that reaches zero in public is the only count that ends this.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Posture as the weapon: what a security force looks like when its objective is that nothing happens — and why the unit that wins this deployment is the one the evening broadcast found boring.

assetDetails.detail: 12 marshals in orange armbands, rotating one per shift per bridgehead, who know every face on the picket line by name. They can clear a bridgehead in 15 minutes and will — if asked first, through the liaison, before the order goes to anyone in uniform. The currency they trade in is being asked first; spend it carefully and it is the best crowd control on the isle.

Not on the constabulary's 11-name suspect list — the paperwork at the quarry was altered by someone who understood it, and the 11 names are the people who did not. Holds the 240kg in divided caches, owns a workboat, and moves only in fog hours. Finding the boat is faster than finding the name.

Commercial mining emulsion — stable, water-resistant, inert without detonators. The same consignment lost 60 detonator caps, a fact the quarry reported separately and quietly. Caps are the scarcer item and the better trail: emulsion keeps for years, but whoever bought, stole, or carries detonators on this isle is countable.
